docs.title: Superluminal API Documentation
docs.text: Use the Superluminal API to consume market data, authenticate a Fogo wallet, fund trading subaccounts, and submit signed trading commands.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Quickstart: choose a tested client bundle and complete a bounded first testnet trade.
  • C++ client: build and run the reference C++ client.
  • Python reference client: install and run the Python client and TUI.
  • Fund an account: request testnet collateral from Superluminal or prepare an address for a manual collateral transfer.
  • TP/SL and reduce-only: protect position quantity, handle manual closes, and reconcile conditional exits.
  • Public API: HTTP and WebSocket requests, responses, pagination, and rejection reasons.

docs.title: Public testnet
docs.text:
Service Endpoint HTTP API https://testnet.slx.fi WebSocket API wss://testnet.slx.fi/ws Fogo RPC https://testnet.fogo.io EVM network Arbitrum Sepolia (421614) EVM RPC https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc

Read market identifiers and scaling metadata from the initial SymbologySnapshot on wss://testnet.slx.fi/ws. Fetch EVM contract addresses from GET https://testnet.slx.fi/v1/evm/addresses; do not hardcode them.

docs.title: Account identity
docs.text:
Your Fogo Ed25519 wallet public key identifies your Superluminal account. Each wallet can own multiple numbered trading subaccounts. Authentication proves control of the wallet; signed commands identify the target subaccount.

Request testnet collateral before placing orders. The public gateway permits one authenticated WebSocket session per wallet, so a newer session preempts an older one.

docs.title: Superluminal Public API
docs.text: This reference defines the public Superluminal HTTP and WebSocket API. For a guided setup, start with the C++ client, Python client, or funding guide.

  • EVM chain: Arbitrum Sepolia (421614)

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text:
• Max inbound frame size: 256 KiB
  • Max inbound text command size: 64 KiB
  • Max signed proof payload size: 512 bytes
  • Per-connection inbound WebSocket message rate limit, including data frames and ping/pong control frames:
  • default rate of 3000 messages/minute
  • default burst capacity of 150 messages
  • deployment and wallet-specific limits may differ
  • exceeded connections are closed with msg_rate_limit_exceeded
  • order-like commands are counted by this same limiter:
    • signed_order
    • signed_cancel
    • signed_modify
    • signed_conditional_group
    • signed_conditional_parent
    • signed_conditional_cancel
  • deposit/withdraw commands are also counted by this same limiter.
  • application-level ping messages and WebSocket ping/pong control frames are counted by this same limiter.
  • invalid or unauthenticated messages are counted before command validation so malformed-message floods cannot bypass the limit.
  • The burst capacity allows brief traffic above the per-minute refill rate; clients must then wait for capacity to refill.
  • Ping/pong:
  • Server sends ping every 20s.
  • Read deadline is 120s and extended on pong.

docs.title: Origin policy
docs.text:
• Browser connections are checked against the deployment's origin allowlist at WebSocket upgrade.
  • Non-browser API clients may omit the Origin header.

docs.title: Integer encoding
docs.text:
Order identifier response encodings are chosen by field, not by the size of each value. JavaScript and TypeScript Number cannot represent every integer above 2^53 - 1; decimal strings preserve 64-bit IDs and can be converted directly to bigint.

The response encodings are:

  • client_instruction_id and original_client_instruction_id are always quoted, unsigned decimal strings, including in TP/SL account snapshots. Clients must reject JSON numbers for these fields and decode them losslessly.
  • external_order_id is always a JSON integer number. Gateway-issued values do not exceed JavaScript's maximum safe integer, 9007199254740991. Clients must reject decimal strings for this field.

The signed binary envelopes still encode these identifiers as little-endian uint64 values before base64 encoding; the rule above applies to JSON fields.

Separately, last_seq on /v1/user-volume and /v1/open-interest, and subaccount_id on /v1/user-volume subaccount records, may be emitted as JSON numbers through 9007199254740991 and decimal strings above that limit. JavaScript and TypeScript clients must preserve those dual-form values as bigint or lossless decimal strings, never Number.

Public request_id64 values reserve bit 63 and therefore cannot exceed 9223372036854775807.

Ordinary order and collateral submission commands restrict subaccount IDs to 0..31, although the signed wire field is uint64. This also applies to user_deposit_address and both subaccounts in a transfer.

docs.title: Numeric units
docs.text:
Price, base quantity, monetary amounts, and rates use different scales:

Value Conversion to human units Market price (price, mark_price, perp_price, TP/SL trigger prices) raw * 10^px_exponent, in quote currency per base unit Base quantity (qty, remaining_qty, filled_qty, settled_qty, reduced_qty, net_qty) raw * 10^(-size_decimals), in base units Collateral, fees, cost basis, PnL, funding amounts raw / 1000000, in USD accounting units Funding rates/indices (premium_e8, max_funding_rate_e8, cum_funding_index_e8, prev_funding_index_e8, last_funding_index_e8) raw / 100000000, a dimensionless rate/index Fee rates and price offsets in *_ppm raw / 1000000, a dimensionless fraction Margin and other rates in *_bps raw / 10000, a dimensionless fraction

The six-decimal monetary scale is fixed across markets. It does not come from px_exponent or size_decimals, and quote: "USDC" does not change it. For example, collateral_balance: 10000000000 means 10000 USD, fee: -1000 means a 0.001 USD rebate, and funding_delta: -25000 means a 0.025 USD funding debit. A funding index of 25000 instead means 0.00025; it is not a USD balance.

The monetary rule applies to:

  • collateral_balance, collateral_delta, collateral_amount, and owe_to_insurance;
  • fee, applied_fee, accrued_fee, pending_fees, and fees_accrued_after;
  • cost_basis, remaining_cost_basis, realized_pnl, and monetary PnL fields;
  • funding_delta, funding_accrued, accrued_funding, and net_funding_after;
  • deposit, withdrawal, and collateral-transfer amounts, including actual_deposit, total_deposit, requested_withdraw_amount, and actual_withdraw_amount.

Signed balances, deltas, fees, position cost basis, PnL, and funding amounts are signed integers; deposit/withdraw request amounts are unsigned. Positive fees are charges and negative fees are rebates. Positive funding amounts are credits and negative funding amounts are debits. net_qty and position cost_basis are signed; an order or fill qty is an unsigned magnitude whose direction comes from side.

AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].collateral_balance already includes accrued fees and funding. Do not subtract accrued_fee or add accrued_funding again when displaying that balance.

Configuration fields explicitly suffixed _usd, such as min_deposit_amount_usd in /v1/config, are human USD amounts, not raw six-decimal integers. Token amounts in EVM transactions use the collateral token's decimals; do not infer arbitrary token precision from market symbology. Vault shares are share counts, not collateral amounts.

JSON integer encoding and numeric scaling are separate rules. Private account monetary fields and most sequence/timestamp fields are JSON numbers; implementations must parse large integers losslessly rather than round them through a JavaScript Number. The string-only instruction-ID rule above still applies.

docs.text:
Returns the public exchange configuration.

Sample response:

  "taker_fee_ppm": 100,
  "maker_fee_ppm": -10,

Market identifiers and scaling metadata are delivered as the initial SymbologySnapshot on every WebSocket connection. They are not exposed over HTTP.

docs.title: GET /v1/evm/addresses
docs.text:
Returns public EVM deployment metadata needed by clients to compute user deposit addresses and submit EVM token transfers.

Sample response:

{
  "version": 1,
  "collateral": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
  "gateway": "0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222",
  "fee_recipient": "0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333",
  "user_deposit_init_code_hash": "0x4444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444"
}

Fields:

  • version: response schema version.
  • collateral: ERC20 collateral token address on the EVM chain.
  • gateway: deployed EVMVault address on the EVM chain.
  • fee_recipient: EVM fee recipient address.
  • user_deposit_init_code_hash: CREATE2 init code hash for UserDeposit.

Status:

  • 200: EVM address metadata is configured.
  • 503: gateway has no EVM address metadata configured.

docs.text:

  "last_seq": 12345,
  "users": [
    {
      "wallet_pubkey": "<base58 wallet>",
      "volume": "1234567890",
      "subaccounts": [
        {
          "subaccount_id": 0,
          "volume": "1234567890"
        }
      ],
      "last_updated": "2026-08-18T12:00:00Z",
      "last_seq": 12340
    }
  ]
}

Status:

  • 200: leaderboard returned.
  • 503: notifier leaderboard source is unavailable.

docs.title: Hyperliquid Compatibility
docs.text:
The gateway exposes a small, public market-data surface intended to be Hyperliquid-compatible.

For lowest latency, clients should prefer the native subscribe_market market-data API over the Hyperliquid compatibility layer. The native stream forwards raw gateway market data without the extra channel wrapping, filtering, and format conversion used by the HL-compatible channels.

Maker/taker behavior:

  • Native subscribe_market exposes raw public book events for both maker and taker books.
  • Raw BookSnapshot, BookDelta, and stream_reset book events are tagged with bookType.
  • Hyperliquid-compatible derived book channels are maker-only:
  • l2Book is built from the maker book only.
  • bbo is built from the maker book only.
  • allMids is computed from maker-book BBOs only.
  • If a client needs taker-book data, it must use the native raw subscribe_market stream and filter by bookType: "taker".

Supported HL-compatible endpoints:

  • POST /info with {"type":"meta"}
  • WebSocket subscribe / unsubscribe for:
  • l2Book
  • bbo
  • trades
  • allMids

This compatibility surface is market-data only. Authentication, private account streaming, and signed order entry use the native Superluminal API.

docs.title: HL WebSocket subscription ack shape
docs.text:
Successful HL-style subscribe commands return:

{
  "channel": "subscriptionResponse",
  "data": {
    "method": "subscribe",
    "subscription": {
      "type": "trades",
      "coin": "BTC"
    }
  }
}

Notes:

  • The response uses a nested data.subscription object.
  • The subscription object reflects the normalized subscription accepted by the gateway.
  • HL-style unsubscribe does not emit an ack; the gateway just stops delivering that channel.

docs.title: Auth gating
docs.text:
• Public commands require no authentication: subscribe_market, unsubscribe_market, native candle commands, Hyperliquid-style l2Book / bbo / trades / allMids subscribe/unsubscribe, and ping.
  • Private/account actions and signed submit require authentication.

docs.title: Auth mode
docs.text: Each WS connection authenticates with wallet challenge mode: auth_wallet -> auth_response.

docs.title: Exactly 1 active authenticated WS per wallet
docs.text:
This gateway enforces one active authenticated WS per bound wallet.

What this means:

  • If a new connection authenticates/binds the same wallet, the previous connection is preempted.
  • The old connection receives:
{
  "type": "session_preempted",
  "reason": "new_session_authenticated"
}
  • Then old connection auth state is cleared and socket is disconnected.

Concrete examples:

  • API bot has wallet W authenticated/bound on WS-1. The same wallet authenticates on WS-2: WS-1 gets session_preempted and disconnects.

docs.title: Symbology bootstrap and updates
docs.text:
Every public WebSocket connection receives one full snapshot when it connects:

{
  "type": "SymbologySnapshot",
  "version": 123,
  "markets": [
    {
      "id": 7,
      "symbol": "BTC",
      "quote": "USDC",
      "pyth_feed_id": 1,
      "max_funding_rate_e8": 10000,
      "px_exponent": -8,
      "tick_size": 100,
      "size_decimals": 5,
      "initial_margin_bps": 500,
      "maintenance_margin_bps": 250,
      "transfer_margin_floor_bps": 1000,
      "status": "active",
      "reduce_only": false,
      "change_count": 4
    }
  ]
}

After the snapshot, each changed market is sent alone:

{
  "type": "SymbologyMarketUpdate",
  "market": {
    "id": 7,
    "symbol": "BTC",
    "quote": "USDC",
    "pyth_feed_id": 1,
    "max_funding_rate_e8": 10000,
    "px_exponent": -8,
    "tick_size": 100,
    "size_decimals": 5,
    "initial_margin_bps": 500,
    "maintenance_margin_bps": 250,
    "transfer_margin_floor_bps": 1000,
    "status": "inactive",
    "reduce_only": false,
    "change_count": 5
  }
}

Clients apply an update only when its change_count is newer than the cached count for that same market id. Counts for different market ids are independent.

Symbology fields:

Field Meaning id, symbol, quote Market ID, base symbol, and quote currency px_exponent Signed price exponent: human price is raw_price * 10^px_exponent size_decimals Base quantity precision: human quantity is raw_qty / 10^size_decimals tick_size Price tick in raw price units; signed-order price validation also enforces the accepted price grid pyth_feed_id Oracle feed identifier max_funding_rate_e8 Maximum funding-rate magnitude, scaled by 100000000 initial_margin_bps, maintenance_margin_bps, transfer_margin_floor_bps Margin rates in basis points (100 means 1%) status active, deactivating, settling, or inactive reduce_only Whether the market restricts trading to reducing positions change_count Market metadata change counter

For the example's px_exponent = -8 and size_decimals = 5, a price of 5000000000000 means 50000 quote units per BTC, and a quantity of 100000 means 1 BTC. Its 50000 USD notional is 50000000000 monetary units. See Numeric units for collateral, fees, PnL, and funding; symbology does not supply a separate monetary exponent.

When a subscribed market becomes inactive, the gateway first sends its SymbologyMarketUpdate, removes every subscription for that market on the connection, and then sends:

{
  "type": "MarketUnsubscribed",
  "market_id": 7,
  "reason": "inactive"
}

Clients choose market subscriptions after processing the initial snapshot and continue processing symbology updates on the same WebSocket connection.

Every connection also receives an ExchangeConfigSnapshot containing the same nine fields as GET /v1/config. Later changes use the identical payload with "type":"ExchangeConfigUpdate".

docs.title: subscribe_market (public)
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "subscribe_market", "symbol": 7 }

Fields:

  • type: literal string subscribe_market
  • symbol: active symbology market id (uint32 on the wire; for example 7)

Success:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "accepted" }

Failure example:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "rejected", "reason": "invalid_symbol" }

Streaming behavior:

  • subscribe_market is the native public raw market-data stream.
  • Raw BookSnapshot, BookDelta, and Trade payloads include the stream sequence in seq.
  • Raw BookSnapshot and BookDelta payloads on this stream carry bookType: "maker" or bookType: "taker".
  • Raw BookSnapshot and BookDelta payloads carry the current oracle-derived mark_price; it is 0 until the matcher has a valid oracle price.
  • Clients should filter book events by bookType if they only want one view.
  • Raw Trade events remain on this stream.
  • Raw FundingIndex events are also delivered on this stream when funding index updates are published for a subscribed market.
  • stream_reset payloads for this stream also carry bookType, and unfiltered recovery may emit one reset for maker and one for taker.

Native BookSnapshot example:

{
  "type": "BookSnapshot",
  "seq": 101,
  "bookType": "maker",
  "id": 7,
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "book_cursor": 5000,
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 2,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1710000000000000000,
  "mark_price": 10001500000,
  "depth_cap": 100,
  "bids": [
    { "price": 10001000000, "qty": 500000, "order_count": 1 }
  ],
  "asks": [
    { "price": 10002000000, "qty": 300000, "order_count": 2 }
  ],
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1710000000000100000
}

Native BookDelta example:

{
  "type": "BookDelta",
  "seq": 102,
  "bookType": "maker",
  "id": 7,
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "prev_book_cursor": 5000,
  "book_cursor": 5001,
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 2,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1710000000001000000,
  "depth_cap": 100,
  "mark_price": 10001500000,
  "bids": [
    { "price": 10001000000, "qty": 700000, "order_count": 2 }
  ],
  "asks": [
    { "price": 10002000000, "qty": 0, "order_count": 0 }
  ],
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1710000000001100000
}

Native Trade example:

{
  "type": "Trade",
  "seq": 103,
  "id": 7,
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 2,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1710000000002000000,
  "trade_id": 77,
  "side": "B",
  "price": 10001500000,
  "qty": 200000,
  "hash": "0",
  "buyer": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "seller": [5, 6, 7, 8],
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1710000000002100000
}

Native FundingIndex example:

{
  "type": "FundingIndex",
  "seq": 104,
  "oracle_price_batch_id": 44,
  "entries": [
    {
      "market_id": 7,
      "perp_price": 10001500000,
      "premium_e8": 250,
      "cum_funding_index_e8": 123456
    }
  ],
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1710000000003100000
}

Notes:

  • price, qty, mark_price, and perp_price are raw integer values interpreted using the market's symbology metadata.
  • premium_e8 and cum_funding_index_e8 are signed fixed-point values scaled by 1e8.
  • Optional fields such as seq, batch_id, term, depth_cap, and truncated are omitted when they have zero or false values.
  • gateway_send_unix_ns is added by the gateway immediately before sending the event to the client.

docs.title: Book synchronization and recovery
docs.text:
Maintain separate books and cursors for each (market id, bookType) pair. A maker snapshot or delta does not establish the taker book's state.

  1. Subscribe after reading symbology. Until a BookSnapshot arrives, the book is unsynchronized; do not use standalone deltas as a complete book.
  2. A snapshot replaces all cached bids and asks for its pair. Store its book_cursor. depth_cap and truncated, when supplied, describe the published view; absence of a level outside that view does not prove there are no orders at that price.
  3. For a delta, require nonzero cursors and prev_book_cursor == stored_book_cursor. Apply it, then store its book_cursor. Cursors need not increase by exactly one. Use the cursor link, not arithmetic on seq, to test book continuity.
  4. Each delta level is the new absolute quantity at its price on that side. Replace that side's quantity; qty = 0 removes that side's level. Prices absent from the delta stay unchanged. For example, a bid of 500000 followed by a delta of 700000 becomes 700000, not 1200000. order_count, when supplied, is also an absolute value.
  5. If the cursor link fails or stream_reset arrives, discard the affected book and cursor, mark it unsynchronized, and send subscribe_market again for that market. Wait for a fresh snapshot. A reset identifies the market in symbol and the affected view in bookType; an unfiltered subscription can receive resets for both views.

The reference clients buffer a bounded number of deltas while awaiting a snapshot and apply only a chain linked from its cursor. An independent client may instead discard those deltas and request another snapshot if it cannot prove continuity. Do not merge unlinked deltas into a fresh snapshot.

On WebSocket disconnect, invalidate the subscribed books. Reconnect, process the new symbology snapshot, and resubscribe to active markets. Trade and FundingIndex are separate events; they do not replace book levels or advance your stored book cursor. seq can skip because other events share the stream. If MarketUnsubscribed reports an inactive market, clear its local book and subscriptions rather than repeatedly resubscribing to that inactive market.

docs.title: unsubscribe_market (public)
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "unsubscribe_market", "symbol": 7 }

Fields:

  • type: literal string unsubscribe_market
  • symbol: market ID to remove from this connection's native subscriptions

Success:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "accepted" }

Unsubscribing is idempotent and does not require the market to remain active. It leaves Hyperliquid-style and candle subscriptions unchanged. MarketUnsubscribed is a separate server notification for market deactivation; it is not the response to this command.

docs.title: Hyperliquid-style l2Book subscribe (public)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "method": "subscribe",
  "subscription": { "type": "l2Book", "coin": "BTC" }
}

Supported subscription fields:

  • type: must be l2Book
  • coin: active market symbol string from symbology, for example BTC
  • nSigFigs: optional, supported values are 2, 3, 4, 5
  • mantissa: optional, only valid when nSigFigs is 5; supported values are 2 or 5

Success response:

{
  "channel": "subscriptionResponse",
  "data": {
    "method": "subscribe",
    "subscription": { "type": "l2Book", "coin": "BTC" }
  }
}

Streaming payloads:

{
  "channel": "l2Book",
  "data": {
    "coin": "BTC",
    "levels": [
      [{"px":"100.01","sz":"5","n":1}],
      [{"px":"100.02","sz":"3","n":2}]
    ],
    "time": 1710000000000
  }
}

Notes:

docs.title: Native candle commands (public)
docs.text:
Supported candle resolutions:

  • Canonical names: 1m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 1d, 1w
  • Accepted aliases: 1, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 120, 240, D, 1D, daily, W, 1W, weekly
  • Missing or empty resolution is accepted as 1m.

The canonical candle resolution is 1m. Higher resolutions are derived from finalized 1m candles.

Requests identify markets with market_id. For legacy clients, if market_id is omitted or 0, the numeric symbol field is used as the market id. Prefer market_id in new clients. Response symbol fields are display symbols such as BTC.

Range request:

{
  "type": "get_candle_range",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "1h"
}

Range response:

{
  "type": "candle_range",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "1h",
  "available": true,
  "oldest_time_unix_s": 1700002800,
  "latest_time_unix_s": 1707685200
}

For derived resolutions, oldest_time_unix_s and latest_time_unix_s are fully complete bucket starts. In-progress derived buckets are not advertised by candle_range. For 1m, all published source candles are already final.

If no candles are available, the response is:

{
  "type": "candle_range",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "1m",
  "available": false
}

Historical request:

{
  "type": "get_candles",
  "request_id": "chart-1",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "5m",
  "from_unix_s": 1707684000,
  "to_unix_s": 1707687600,
  "limit": 500
}

get_candles fields:

  • from_unix_s and to_unix_s are required, nonzero Unix seconds. from_unix_s must be less than to_unix_s.
  • The range is half-open: [from_unix_s, to_unix_s).
  • limit is optional. 0 or an omitted value uses the default 5000. The maximum accepted limit is 10000.
  • Candles are returned in ascending time_unix_s order.

Historical response:

{
  "type": "candles",
  "request_id": "chart-1",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "5m",
  "from_unix_s": 1707684000,
  "to_unix_s": 1707687600,
  "available": true,
  "partial": false,
  "candles": [
    {
      "time_unix_s": 1707684000,
      "symbol": "BTC",
      "open": 1000000,
      "high": 1010000,
      "low": 990000,
      "close": 1005000,
      "volume": 250000,
      "trade_count": 42,
      "first_trade_id": 100,
      "last_trade_id": 141,
      "first_trade_unix_ns": 1707684000123456789,
      "last_trade_unix_ns": 1707684059123456789,
      "source_market_data_seq": 12345,
      "is_final": true
    }
  ]
}

get_candles may include the current in-progress derived bucket when the requested range reaches the latest available data; that candle has is_final: false.

If no candles are available, the gateway returns a candles event with available: false, partial: false, and an empty candles array. reason may be present:

  • stream_unavailable: no retained candle stream is available for the requested market.
  • history_unavailable: historical candles are temporarily unavailable.

partial: true means the returned set is incomplete. This can happen when the response is truncated by limit or only part of the requested range is temporarily available.

Per-candle optional fields:

  • symbol: present when known.
  • first_trade_id, last_trade_id, first_trade_unix_ns, last_trade_unix_ns: omitted when the candle has no trades or the source did not provide those values.

Live subscribe:

{
  "type": "subscribe_candles",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "5m"
}

Live candle event:

{
  "type": "candle",
  "market_id": 1,
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "resolution": "5m",
  "seq": 100,
  "app_seq": 100,
  "time_unix_s": 1707684000,
  "open": 1000000,
  "high": 1010000,
  "low": 990000,
  "close": 1005000,
  "volume": 250000,
  "trade_count": 42,
  "first_trade_id": 100,
  "last_trade_id": 141,
  "first_trade_unix_ns": 1707684000123456789,
  "last_trade_unix_ns": 1707684059123456789,
  "source_market_data_seq": 12345,
  "is_final": false
}

For derived live subscriptions, updates have is_final: false while the derived bucket is open. A final update with is_final: true is emitted when the bucket completes. unsubscribe_candles uses the same market_id and resolution fields.

Candle command rejects use the normal ack rejection shape:

  • invalid_candle_subscription: request JSON is malformed or contains unknown fields.
  • invalid_resolution: resolution is not one of the supported values above.
  • invalid_symbol: the requested market id is not active.
  • invalid_candle_range: get_candles has missing/zero bounds or from_unix_s >= to_unix_s.
  • candle_limit_too_large: get_candles.limit > 10000.

docs.title: auth_wallet (start wallet challenge)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "auth_wallet",
  "wallet_pubkey": "<base58>",
  "expiry_seconds": 300
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string auth_wallet
  • wallet_pubkey: required Solana public key in base58
  • expiry_seconds: required integer; 0 means never expire, otherwise must be > 60

Rules:

  • expiry_seconds is required.
  • expiry_seconds = 0 means the wallet-auth session does not expire by gateway TTL.
  • Positive expiry_seconds values must be > 60.
  • wallet_pubkey is required.
  • This is the only command that issues wallet challenges.

On success:

  • auth_challenge event
  • then ack accepted

The challenge is sent before the accepted ack on the WebSocket.

{
  "type": "auth_challenge",
  "wallet_pubkey": "<wallet>",
  "nonce": "<nonce>",
  "issued_unix_ms": 1710000000000,
  "expires_unix_ms": 1710000060000,
  "session_id": "<gateway_session_id>",
  "message": "AETHON_AUTH_V1|<wallet_pubkey>|<nonce>|<iat>|<exp>|<session_id>"
}

docs.title: auth_response (complete wallet challenge)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "auth_response",
  "wallet_pubkey": "<optional wallet pubkey>",
  "nonce": "<challenge nonce>",
  "signature_b64": "<ed25519 signature over challenge message bytes>",
  "signed_payload_b64": "<optional Ledger V0 signed payload bytes>",
  "is_delegate": true
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string auth_response
  • wallet_pubkey: optional base58 pubkey; if supplied it must match the challenged wallet
  • nonce: exact nonce from auth_challenge
  • signature_b64: base64-encoded ed25519 signature over the exact auth_challenge.message bytes
  • signed_payload_b64: optional base64-encoded Solana off-chain V0 signed payload. When present, the Ledger prefix and body are verified and the signature is checked over the full signed payload.
  • is_delegate: optional boolean; when true, the signature must verify with the wallet's current delegate key

Rules:

  • Challenge TTL is 60s.
  • Challenge is single-use (replay rejected).
  • Without is_delegate, signature must verify against the challenged wallet pubkey and exact challenge message.
  • With is_delegate: true, the signature must verify with the challenged wallet's currently registered delegate key.
  • On success, wallet is automatically bound for signed-submit authorization.
  • Delegate-authenticated sessions may submit orders, cancels, modifies, vault operations, and subaccount transfers.
  • Collateral withdraw requires owner wallet authentication; delegate-authenticated sessions are rejected for signed_withdraw.

Delegate rotation warning:

  • Before changing a wallet's delegate key, cancel all open orders for that wallet.
  • Existing resting orders are not automatically canceled when the delegate changes.
  • Orders signed by a previous delegate may fail settlement after the delegate key is updated.

Success:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "accepted" }

docs.title: Ledger Hardware Wallet Signing
docs.text:
Ledger Solana hardware wallets sign Solana off-chain message payloads, not the raw gateway message bytes. Ledger clients should use Solana off-chain message V0 signing.

V0 signed payload layout:

0xff || "solana offchain" ||
version(1) ||
app_domain(32) ||
format(1) ||
signer_count(1) ||
signer_pubkey(32) ||
message_len_le_u16(2) ||
message_body

Gateway Ledger clients use:

version = 0
app_domain = "aethon-gateway" padded with zero bytes to 32 bytes
format = 0
signer_count = 1
signer_pubkey = wallet pubkey bytes

The V0 prefix before message_body is 85 bytes.

Auth challenge Ledger body:

AETHON_AUTH_V1|<wallet_pubkey>|<nonce>|<iat>|<exp>|<session_id>

This is the exact auth_challenge.message encoded as UTF-8.

signed_set_delegate Ledger body:

base64(owner_pubkey || delegate_key || delegate_nonce_le_u64 || request_id64_le_u64 || iat_le_u64 || exp_le_u64)

The base64 wrapper is used because the set-delegate payload contains binary bytes, while Ledger Solana off-chain V0 message bodies must be valid text.

collateral_balance in AccountSnapshot and UserCollateralUpdate is the net user-visible collateral for that subaccount. It reflects the current collateral after fees and funding paid or accrued. AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].accrued_fee is the total accrued fee included in that net value, and AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].accrued_funding is the total accrued funding included in that net value.

AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].status is one of active, liquidating, or delinquent. A delinquent subaccount also includes owe_to_insurance with the current amount owed to insurance.

AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].positions[].realized_pnl, funding_accrued, last_funding_index_e8, and pending_fees are emitted as numeric fields for every position. If a historical value is unavailable, the field is emitted as 0.

AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].working_orders[].filled_qty is required and is the cumulative quantity filled for that order across auctions. Quantity removed by a modify is not included. execution_mode is also required: user orders use 0 for normal and 4 for reduce-only; modes 1–3 are system modes. Preserve it when reconstructing a working order after reconnect; a modify must use the order's original execution mode.

AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].conditional_groups contains approved TP/SL groups that have not emitted a terminal lifecycle event at the snapshot sequence. Triggered groups remain visible as triggering while the active child or terminal outputs are being resolved. Groups awaiting a rearm approval remain visible as dormant or waiting_fill. Groups whose initial approval has not been published are omitted. activation_mode is parent_fill when settled parent fills add protected quantity, or immediate when the submitted quantity protects the current position without a parent order. leg_flags uses bit 1 for take profit and bit 2 for stop loss; trigger-source fields use bit 1 for oracle and bit 2 for auction.

Private stream events are authoritative; signed submit commands do not emit an immediate success acknowledgement. Event types include:

  • Account bootstrap/errors: AccountSnapshot, AccountSnapshotError
  • Order lifecycle: OrderAccepted, ConditionalApproved, ConditionalTriggered, ConditionalExpired, ConditionalCancelled, ConditionalInvalidated, ConditionalCompleted, OrderReject, CancelAck, CancelReject, ModifyAck, ModifyReject
  • Fills and settlement: Fill, FillSettled, FillBusted
  • Collateral and funding: UserDepositAddressStatus, UserCollateralUpdate, AccountFundingUpdate
  • Liquidation status: LiquidationTriggered, LiquidationCleared
  • Withdraw settlement: WithdrawStatus
  • Vault and transfer settlement: CreateVaultStatus, CreateVault, DepositVaultStatus, DepositVault, WithdrawVaultStatus, WithdrawVault, TransferSubaccountStatus, SetDelegateStatus, VaultOperationSubaccountCollateralChange

docs.title: Account synchronization and recovery
docs.text:
Authentication and subscribe_account acknowledgements do not establish account readiness. Wait for a valid AccountSnapshot before making decisions from balances, positions, working orders, or conditional groups.

  • Treat the snapshot as replacement state for the authenticated wallet, including its arrays of subaccounts, positions, working orders, and TP/SL groups. Remove cached entries absent from the new snapshot. Set the account state watermark to last_seq; do not apply already-covered fills again.
  • Apply subsequent account-state lifecycle events only when their seq is greater than that watermark, then advance it. Sequences are not contiguous for one wallet: a jump by more than one is not by itself an account gap. Public book seq and private account sequences are not interchangeable.
  • UserDepositAddressStatus is an exception: it acknowledges a registration command, which the account snapshot does not represent. It can arrive with seq <= last_seq. Still correlate and process that acknowledgement by subaccount and request timestamps, without moving the state watermark backward or changing balances from it.
  • The gateway can send a fresh account snapshot when its upstream recovers, even while your WebSocket remains connected. Install a newer snapshot as replacement state. Ignore older snapshots within the same session. On a new session, bootstrap from the fresh snapshot rather than treating the old cached state as current.
  • On disconnect, suspend new submissions, reconnect, authenticate, and send subscribe_account again. Reconcile the fresh snapshot and synchronized market data before resuming. AccountSnapshotError means bootstrap has failed; an earlier accepted acknowledgement does not make that account ready. session_preempted means another authenticated session owns the wallet; stop instead of competing in a reconnect loop.

The public subscription has no start_seq replay parameter. A fresh snapshot recovers current state, not every event missed during the disconnect. Use get_order_history and get_order_events to reconcile terminal orders and missed fills/settlements, and get_funding_history for funding records. History pagination has its own cursors; it does not advance the live account watermark.

Persist submitted instruction IDs and observed order IDs so an ambiguous disconnect can be reconciled. Check working orders, conditional groups, and history before retrying an order, cancel, or TP/SL command. An order absent from working_orders may already have filled, expired, or been cancelled. A client instruction ID correlates a command; do not assume that resending it provides an exactly-once submission guarantee.

Track each fill leg by wallet, subaccount, external order ID, and trade_id when available. Fill, FillSettled, and FillBusted are different stages of that same fill, not duplicate messages. Do not discard a settlement because its trade ID was already seen in a provisional fill, or merge two order legs of the same trade. Use the live sequence watermark to avoid applying the same state event twice; use order history when a legacy event lacks a trade ID.

For a reduce-only result, FillSettled remains one event at one seq and keeps qty and fee as the provisional matched quantity and requested fee. It additionally includes trade_id, settled_qty, reduced_qty, applied_fee, adjustment_reason: "reduce_only", and three per-order-leg booleans: reduce_only_leg, limiting_leg, and exhausted_leg. These booleans identify whether this account's leg was reduce-only, constrained the settled quantity, and consumed all of its on-chain reduce-only capacity, respectively. The quantity invariant is qty = settled_qty + reduced_qty; zero and false values are emitted explicitly.

Use settled_qty and applied_fee to reconcile actual position changes and fees; qty and fee remain provisional. See TP/SL and reduce-only for settlement and manual-close examples.

String enum values in private account events use:

  • side: BID or ASK
  • role: MAKER or TAKER
  • tif: GTC or IOC

docs.title: Private order and fill event schemas
docs.text:
The following field definitions cover ordinary order acceptance, provisional fills, terminal settlement, busts, and cancellation. The reference-client bundles also include typed parsers; these tables describe the gateway payload, including fields a particular client may ignore.

All numeric types below are JSON integer numbers unless explicitly marked as strings. uint64 is unsigned; int64 and int32 are signed. Decode large numbers losslessly. Prices and quantities use symbology; monetary values use the fixed six-decimal scale.

Common envelope fields:

Field Type / presence Definition type string, required Event discriminant seq uint64, required Private account-state sequence; see account recovery subaccount_id uint64, required Affected subaccount in the authenticated wallet wallet array of four uint64 words Wallet's 32-byte public key, split into four little-endian words symbol uint32 Symbology market ID; present for the order/fill events below external_order_id JSON integer Affected order ID; present for ordinary order/fill events, safe through 9007199254740991 client_instruction_id unsigned decimal string, optional Request ID; omitted when zero/unavailable, including ordinary settlement messages client_unix_ns, gateway_recv_unix_ns, sequencer_recv_unix_ns, matcher_unix_ns uint64, optional Client, gateway receipt, sequencer receipt, and matcher timestamps, respectively, in Unix nanoseconds gateway_send_unix_ns uint64 Unix nanoseconds when the gateway sends the event global_seq, batch_id, term, batch_marker_unix_ns uint64, optional Source sequence, auction batch, sequencing term, and batch-marker Unix nanoseconds; diagnostic metadata flags uint16, optional Source event flags; reserved for event-specific interpretation auction uint8, optional Source auction metadata; omitted when zero

The shared envelope also includes the following numeric fields:

Field Type Meaning for these events order_type uint8 Order kind on acceptance; otherwise an unused zero unless specified price uint64 Order/fill price where defined; unused zero on cancel outcomes delta_ppm int32 Order offset/protection on acceptance; otherwise unused zero execution_mode uint8 Order mode on acceptance/fill; otherwise unused zero status, error_code uint8, uint32 Terminal settlement result where defined; otherwise unused zeros vault_id, position_index, phase uint32, uint16, uint8 Unused zeros for these ordinary order/fill events

The shared serializer emits order_type, price, delta_ppm, execution_mode, status, error_code, vault_id, position_index, and phase even when their value is zero. Interpret them only where the event definition gives them meaning. For example, status: 0 on OrderAccepted does not mean the order has settled, and order_type: 0 on a Fill does not establish the original order type.

Other optional numeric/string fields are normally omitted when zero/empty. For example, an absent fee means zero, and an absent cancel reason means zero. Two exceptions are always explicit: matcher Fill.remaining_qty, including zero, and all reduce-only settlement adjustment fields, including zero quantities/fees and false booleans. Ignore unknown response fields for forward compatibility; request envelopes retain their documented strict JSON validation.

docs.title: OrderAccepted
docs.text:
Creates an accepted order with its original parameters. It is not a fill or a settlement. Correlate the request by client_instruction_id, then track the order by external_order_id.

docs.title: Fill
docs.text:
A regular fill is provisional until its corresponding FillSettled or FillBusted. One order can produce multiple fills and terminal settlement messages, each correlated by its order ID and trade ID.

Field Type / presence Definition trade_id uint64, when available Trade identity used to correlate this fill leg with settlement side BID / ASK Buy / sell direction for this account role MAKER / TAKER Role for a regular matcher fill tif GTC / IOC, optional Original order time in force price uint64, required Raw auction fill price qty uint64, positive Raw provisional matched quantity remaining_qty uint64, required for matcher fills Raw order quantity remaining after this match; zero is emitted fee int64, optional Provisional requested fee in six-decimal USD; negative is a rebate execution_mode uint8, required Order execution mode; 4 identifies a reduce-only order leg reason uint32, optional 0 = regular, 1 = ADL; zero can be omitted 
{
  "type": "Fill",
  "seq": 12347,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "client_instruction_id": "9001",
  "trade_id": 77,
  "side": "BID",
  "role": "MAKER",
  "tif": "GTC",
  "order_type": 0,
  "execution_mode": 0,
  "price": 5000000000000,
  "qty": 40000,
  "remaining_qty": 60000,
  "fee": -200000,
  "delta_ppm": 0,
  "status": 0,
  "error_code": 0,
  "vault_id": 0,
  "position_index": 0,
  "phase": 0,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000200000
}

System-generated fills can carry liquidation execution modes. In particular, an ADL outcome uses type: "Fill", reason: 1, and role: "target" or "counterparty". It is emitted after successful ADL settlement, rather than as an ordinary provisional matcher fill. external_order_id, client_instruction_id, and remaining_qty may be absent for a leg without an order. Additional ADL fields are market_id (uint32), request_seq, operation_nonce, and batch_id (uint64), allocated_loss (unsigned six-decimal USD), counterparty_wallet (four uint64 words), counterparty_subaccount_id (uint64), and onchain_signature (base58 string), when available. Do not wait for an ordinary FillSettled for this already-settled ADL event.

docs.title: FillSettled and FillBusted
docs.text:
These messages resolve a regular provisional fill. They repeat its order, market, side, price, quantity, fee, and trade identity; they do not normally carry its client_instruction_id, role, or tif.

Field Type / presence Definition trade_id uint64, when available Original trade identity side BID / ASK Original fill direction price uint64, required Original raw fill price qty uint64, positive Original provisional matched quantity fee int64, optional Original requested fee in six-decimal USD; omitted at zero status uint8, required 0 = finalized, 1 = error; retry status 2 does not emit a terminal fill message error_code uint32, required Zero on successful settlement; numeric failure code otherwise error_domain, error, error_message strings, optional Error subsystem, machine-readable name, and description, when the code is recognized onchain_signature base58 string, optional SVM transaction signature when available; a signature alone does not prove success

Ordinary successful settlement:

{
  "type": "FillSettled",
  "seq": 12348,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "trade_id": 77,
  "side": "BID",
  "price": 5000000000000,
  "qty": 40000,
  "fee": -200000,
  "order_type": 0,
  "delta_ppm": 0,
  "execution_mode": 0,
  "status": 0,
  "error_code": 0,
  "vault_id": 0,
  "position_index": 0,
  "phase": 0,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689601000000000
}

A failed settlement has the same base shape, with type: "FillBusted" and its actual status and error_code, for example:

{
  "type": "FillBusted",
  "seq": 12348,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "trade_id": 77,
  "side": "BID",
  "price": 5000000000000,
  "qty": 40000,
  "fee": -200000,
  "order_type": 0,
  "delta_ppm": 0,
  "execution_mode": 0,
  "status": 1,
  "error_code": 1,
  "vault_id": 0,
  "position_index": 0,
  "phase": 0,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689601000000000
}

For ordinary FillSettled, commit the provisional quantity and fee once. For FillBusted, remove the provisional position/fee effect if your application applied it; do not treat the fill as settled. A bust does not itself establish that the order is open again. Reconcile working-order state from its lifecycle, snapshot, or history.

A reduce-only FillSettled adds the following required fields to that same base shape; it does not emit a separate bust for reduced_qty:

Field Type Definition adjustment_reason literal "reduce_only" Identifies the atomic settlement adjustment settled_qty uint64 Quantity that actually settled reduced_qty uint64 Quantity removed from the provisional match; qty = settled_qty + reduced_qty applied_fee int64 Actual fee/rebate in six-decimal USD reduce_only_leg boolean This account's order leg was reduce-only limiting_leg boolean This leg constrained the settled quantity exhausted_leg boolean This leg consumed its remaining on-chain reduce-only capacity

trade_id is required for these adjusted messages. Replace the provisional effect with settled_qty and applied_fee, including when they are zero. See TP/SL and reduce-only for examples.

docs.title: CancelAck and CancelReject
docs.text:
CancelAck removes the order's remaining working quantity. Already matched fills can still settle or bust afterward. It can acknowledge an explicit cancel or report automatic cancellation, such as IOC remainder expiry. CancelReject rejects the cancel request; it does not cancel the order.

Field Type / presence Definition client_instruction_id unsigned decimal string, optional Cancel request ID; automatic cancels can carry the original order request ID original_client_instruction_id unsigned decimal string, optional Original order request ID, when the owner has the order's metadata reason uint32, optional at zero Cancellation/rejection reason from the table below side, role, tif strings, optional Order metadata when available; an unknown-order rejection does not establish these parameters qty uint64, optional at zero Remaining raw quantity removed by a successful cancel, or affected order quantity when available original_qty uint64, optional Original raw order quantity original_iat, original_exp uint64, optional Original proof issuance/expiry in Unix seconds 
{
  "type": "CancelAck",
  "seq": 12349,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "client_instruction_id": "9002",
  "original_client_instruction_id": "9001",
  "side": "BID",
  "role": "MAKER",
  "tif": "GTC",
  "qty": 60000,
  "original_qty": 100000,
  "original_iat": 1735689600,
  "original_exp": 1735776000,
  "order_type": 0,
  "price": 0,
  "delta_ppm": 0,
  "execution_mode": 0,
  "status": 0,
  "error_code": 0,
  "vault_id": 0,
  "position_index": 0,
  "phase": 0,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689602000000000
}

For CancelReject, the base envelope instead has type: "CancelReject" and a nonzero reason. For example, an unknown-order rejection is:

{
  "type": "CancelReject",
  "seq": 12350,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "client_instruction_id": "9003",
  "reason": 1,
  "side": "BID",
  "role": "MAKER",
  "tif": "IOC",
  "order_type": 0,
  "price": 0,
  "delta_ppm": 0,
  "execution_mode": 0,
  "status": 0,
  "error_code": 0,
  "vault_id": 0,
  "position_index": 0,
  "phase": 0,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689603000000000
}

In an unknown-order rejection, default side, role, and tif values are not evidence of the original order's parameters. Other order metadata may be absent. Conditional-group cancel rejection uses the group ID in external_order_id and echoes the cancel request's client_instruction_id; successful group cancellation emits ConditionalCancelled.

reason Meaning 0 or absent Successful explicit cancel 1 Unknown order 2 IOC remainder expired 3 Missing symbology 4 Cancel role does not match order role 5 Order expired 6 Liquidation triggered cancellation 7 Market inactive 8 OCO sibling activated 9 Conditional position invalidated 10 Conditional group expired 11 Conditional group cancelled 12 Conditional group completed

These reasons are shared by cancellation outcomes: the event's type determines whether the order was cancelled or the request was rejected.

UserCollateralUpdate example:

{
  "type": "UserCollateralUpdate",
  "seq": 12346,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "collateral_delta": 1000000,
  "collateral_balance": 124456789,
  "fee": 0,
  "actual_deposit": 1000000,
  "total_deposit": 1000000,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000100000
}

UserDepositAddressStatus is emitted after deposit-address registration completes. It echoes the request timestamps for correlation:

{
  "type": "UserDepositAddressStatus",
  "seq": 12345,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "client_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000,
  "gateway_recv_unix_ns": 1735689600000001000,
  "sequencer_recv_unix_ns": 1735689600000002000,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000003000
}

OrderReject.reason is a numeric order-reject code. Risk rejections use these detailed codes:

  • 1 = MissingSymbology
  • 2 = Full
  • 3 = RiskRejected (legacy generic risk rejection)
  • 4 = RiskRejectedLiquidationNotActive — account is not liquidating
  • 5 = RiskRejectedSubaccountNotActive — account is inactive or liquidating
  • 6 = RiskRejectedInsufficientFreeCollateral — insufficient free collateral
  • 7 = RiskRejectedMarketInactive — market is inactive
  • 8 = ConditionalUnknownSubaccount
  • 13 = ConditionalInvalidGroup
  • 14 = ConditionalFull
  • 16 = ConditionalOwnerConflict

Clients should treat unknown numeric values as distinct reject reasons rather than coercing them to a generic error. Synchronous preflight rejections use a string reason instead (for example, "Permission Denied").

ConditionalApproved is emitted after Bop durably admits a conditional group. It identifies the group and each enabled dormant leg:

{
  "type": "ConditionalApproved",
  "version": 1,
  "activation_mode": "parent_fill",
  "state": "waiting_parent",
  "seq": 12345,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "client_instruction_id": "9009",
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "side": "ASK",
  "group_external_order_id": 101,
  "take_profit_external_order_id": 99,
  "stop_loss_external_order_id": 100,
  "leg_flags": 3,
  "tp_trigger_sources": 3,
  "sl_trigger_sources": 2,
  "tp_trigger_price": 110,
  "sl_trigger_price": 90,
  "qty": 5,
  "expiry_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000
}

ConditionalApproved.qty and snapshot group qty retain the original signed group quantity, including on rearm approvals; they are not the remaining protected quantity. Ordinary child events use the active ID supplied by ConditionalTriggered, while a dormant sibling's CancelAck uses its dormant leg ID. Use conditional lifecycle events to reconcile group state.

  • ConditionalTriggered identifies the selected TP or SL with selected_leg (1 for take profit, 2 for stop loss) and selected_external_order_id. Each trigger assigns a fresh active child ID, replacing that leg's dormant ID, even on the first trigger. It means activation has started, not that the selected order has been accepted into the book. Use this ID for fills and active-child cancellation.
  • ConditionalExpired means dormant protection or its active child expired.
  • ConditionalCancelled reports group or active-child cancellation, including cancellation of an SL's unfilled IOC remainder; original_client_instruction_id is the original group submission. client_instruction_id identifies the explicit cancellation request, or the active child's client instruction for automatic IOC cancellation.
  • ConditionalInvalidated means an activated child was rejected, the parent was modified, or a reduce-only settlement exhausted the protected position.
  • A repeated ConditionalApproved after ConditionalTriggered means Bop has begun another cycle: dormant with residual protected quantity in either activation mode, or waiting_fill pending further settled parent fills.
  • ConditionalCompleted means no protected exposure remains after the parent became terminal, or an immediate group's exit completed its protection. Parent rejection or cancellation also completes an unprotected group once no parent fills remain pending settlement.

Each terminal lifecycle event identifies the group with group_external_order_id and removes it from subsequent account snapshots. Per-leg CancelAck events and a triggered leg's normal OrderAccepted or OrderReject continue independently. Every conditional lifecycle event and conditional group in an account snapshot has version: 1. Clients must reject unsupported versions.

AccountFundingUpdate example:

{
  "type": "AccountFundingUpdate",
  "seq": 12347,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "market_id": 7,
  "prev_funding_index_e8": 1000,
  "last_funding_index_e8": 1250,
  "funding_delta": -25,
  "funding_accrued": -25,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000200000
}

LiquidationTriggered example:

{
  "type": "LiquidationTriggered",
  "seq": 12348,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "batch_id": 88,
  "account_status": "liquidating",
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000300000
}

LiquidationCleared example:

{
  "type": "LiquidationCleared",
  "seq": 12349,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "batch_id": 89,
  "account_status": "delinquent",
  "owe_to_insurance": 2500000,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000400000
}

ModifyAck example:

{
  "type": "ModifyAck",
  "seq": 12346,
  "global_seq": 12346,
  "batch_id": 88,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000,
  "symbol": 7,
  "side": "BID",
  "role": "MAKER",
  "tif": "GTC",
  "order_type": 1,
  "client_instruction_id": "9005",
  "original_client_instruction_id": "9001",
  "subaccount_id": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "client_unix_ns": 1735689599999000000,
  "gateway_recv_unix_ns": 1735689599999500000,
  "sequencer_recv_unix_ns": 1735689599999700000,
  "price": 5000100,
  "qty": 2000,
  "delta_ppm": 25,
  "execution_mode": 0
}

ModifyReject has the same order identity fields plus reason; price, qty, and delta_ppm are the rejected requested values when present:

{
  "type": "ModifyReject",
  "seq": 12347,
  "global_seq": 12347,
  "batch_id": 88,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000,
  "symbol": 7,
  "side": "BID",
  "role": "MAKER",
  "tif": "GTC",
  "order_type": 1,
  "client_instruction_id": "9006",
  "original_client_instruction_id": "9001",
  "subaccount_id": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "reason": 2,
  "price": 5000200,
  "qty": 2000,
  "delta_ppm": 30
}

Modify reject reason codes:

  • 1 = UnknownOrder
  • 2 = RoleMismatch
  • 3 = IOCNotModifiable
  • 4 = MarketNotModifiable
  • 5 = InvalidQty
  • 6 = InvalidPrice
  • 7 = Full
  • 8 = MissingSymbology
  • 10 = ExecutionModeMismatch

Code 9 is reserved for conditional-order modify rejection.

docs.title: get_order_history (private, paginated)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "get_order_history",
  "request_id": "hist-1",
  "created_from_unix_s": 1735689600,
  "created_to_unix_s": 1738368000,
  "cursor": "",
  "limit": 20
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string get_order_history
  • request_id: optional caller-supplied correlation id; echoed back in the response so multiple in-flight pages can be matched up
  • created_from_unix_s: optional inclusive lower bound on order creation time, as UTC Unix seconds
  • created_to_unix_s: optional exclusive upper bound on order creation time, as UTC Unix seconds
  • cursor: optional opaque string from the previous page's next_cursor; empty or omitted returns the newest page
  • limit: optional page size; clamped to 1..100, defaults to 20

Rules:

  • Requires an authenticated wallet-bound session (same gating as subscribe_account).
  • Orders are returned for the authenticated bound wallet only; the request does not accept a wallet override.
  • Creation-time filtering uses the half-open interval [created_from_unix_s, created_to_unix_s). Either bound may be omitted for an open-ended query. Supplied bounds must be non-negative integers, and created_from_unix_s must be less than created_to_unix_s when both are present. JSON null is invalid; omit an unused bound instead.
  • next_cursor binds the first page's creation-time bounds. Later pages may omit the bounds and use the cursor alone. If either bound is supplied with a cursor, it must match the bound encoded in that cursor.
  • Strict JSON: unknown fields are rejected with invalid_get_order_history.

Response (one order_history event per request, then ack accepted):

{
  "type": "order_history",
  "request_id": "hist-1",
  "next_cursor": "AgAAAAAAADA-AAAAAAAAMD4AAAAAAAHiQAAAAAcDAAAAAGd0hYAAAAAAZ51kAA",
  "orders": [
    {
      "external_order_id": 123456,
      "client_instruction_id": "9001",
      "subaccount_id": 0,
      "symbol": 7,
      "side": "BID",
      "role": "TAKER",
      "tif": "GTC",
      "order_type": 0,
      "execution_mode": 0,
      "status": "filled",
      "original_iat": 1735689600,
      "created_unix_ns": 1735689600123456789,
      "closed_unix_ns": 1735689601000000000,
      "price": 5000100,
      "original_qty": 2000,
      "remaining_qty": 0,
      "filled_qty": 2000,
      "settled_qty": 2000,
      "busted_qty": 0,
      "reduced_qty": 0,
      "delta_ppm": 0,
      "last_event_seq": 12350
    }
  ]
}

Notes:

  • Orders are ordered most-recent-first by last_event_seq (i.e. by the seq of the last persisted history event for the order).
  • next_cursor is omitted when there are no more rows; pass it back verbatim in the next request to page older.
  • A cursor preserves the first page's event-sequence snapshot and creation-time bounds. Events persisted after that snapshot are excluded from later pages and appear when pagination is restarted without a cursor.
  • Pagination is by distinct order. The page selects orders by last_event_seq and returns one flat row per order.
  • status is one of open, filled, canceled, rejected.
  • execution_mode preserves the accepted order's mode (4 for reduce-only) when present in persisted history; older rows may omit it.
  • side is BID for buys and ASK for sells, matching working_orders and Fill events.
  • price, original_qty, remaining_qty, filled_qty, settled_qty, busted_qty, and reduced_qty are raw integers interpreted using the market's symbology metadata, identical to other private/account events.
  • filled_qty, settled_qty, busted_qty, and reduced_qty are aggregated from persisted fill/settlement events for the order. reduced_qty is quantity removed by reduce-only settlement and is distinct from a failed-settlement bust.
  • Conditional child rows include conditional_group_external_order_id and conditional_leg (1 = TP, 2 = SL) when their association is available. These fields link each active child ID to its group across trigger cycles.
  • event_reason_code and reject_reason_code on the top-level order mirror the latest terminal reason when available.
  • Detailed lifecycle events are fetched separately with get_order_events.

Common rejects:

  • auth_required (no active authenticated WS session)
  • invalid_get_order_history (malformed request payload)
  • invalid_order_history_cursor (cursor is malformed, unsupported, or conflicts with an explicitly supplied creation-time bound)
  • invalid_order_history_created_from (created_from_unix_s is null or not a non-negative integer)
  • invalid_order_history_created_to (created_to_unix_s is null or not a non-negative integer)
  • invalid_order_history_created_range (equal or inverted creation-time bounds)
  • stream_unavailable (the account-history service is unavailable)
  • order_history_unavailable (the order-history request failed)

Rejected ack responses echo request_id when supplied.

docs.title: get_order_events (private, paginated)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "get_order_events",
  "request_id": "order-events-1",
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "market_id": 7,
  "cursor": "",
  "limit": 20
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string get_order_events
  • request_id: optional caller-supplied correlation id; echoed back in the response so multiple in-flight pages can be matched up
  • external_order_id: required JSON integer order id from the private order stream; decimal strings are rejected
  • market_id: required market id for the order
  • cursor: optional opaque string from the previous page's next_cursor; empty or omitted returns the newest page
  • limit: optional page size; clamped to 1..100, defaults to 20

Rules:

  • Requires an authenticated wallet-bound session (same gating as subscribe_account).
  • Events are returned for the authenticated bound wallet only; the request does not accept a wallet override.
  • external_order_id and market_id must both be greater than 0.
  • Strict JSON: unknown fields are rejected with invalid_get_order_events.

Response (one order_events event per request, then ack accepted):

{
  "type": "order_events",
  "request_id": "order-events-1",
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "market_id": 7,
  "next_cursor": "12348",
  "events": [
    {
      "event_type": "settled",
      "client_instruction_id": "0",
      "price": 5000050,
      "qty": 2000,
      "fee": -3,
      "settlement_seq": 55,
      "event_unix_ns": 1735689601000000000,
      "stream_seq": 12350
    },
    {
      "event_type": "filled",
      "client_instruction_id": "9001",
      "trade_id": 77,
      "price": 5000050,
      "qty": 2000,
      "remaining_qty": 0,
      "event_unix_ns": 1735689600999000000,
      "stream_seq": 12348
    }
  ]
}

Notes:

  • Events are ordered newest-first by stream_seq.
  • next_cursor is omitted when there are no more rows; pass it back verbatim in the next request to page older.
  • events[].event_type is one of accepted, modified, filled, cancelled, rejected, settled, busted, reduced, cancel_rejected, modify_rejected.
  • events[].price is the order price for accepted, the new requested price for modified, the fill/settlement price for filled / settled / busted / reduced, and may be omitted for events without a price.
  • events[].qty is the order quantity for accepted, the new requested quantity for modified, the fill/settlement quantity for filled / settled / busted / reduced, and the affected quantity for cancel/reject events when available.
  • events[].reason_code is present for rejected/cancelled/reject events when a reason is available.
  • events[].fee is present on settlement-derived events when available. Fill events can omit fee because fees are finalized with settlement events.
  • events[].conditional_group_external_order_id and conditional_leg (1 = TP, 2 = SL) identify an associated conditional child when available.

Common rejects:

  • auth_required (no active authenticated WS session)
  • invalid_get_order_events (malformed request payload)
  • stream_unavailable (the account-history service is unavailable)
  • order_events_unavailable (the order-events request failed)

Rejected ack responses echo request_id when supplied.

docs.title: get_vault_accounts (private, paginated)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "get_vault_accounts",
  "request_id": "vaults-1",
  "cursor": "",
  "limit": 20
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string get_vault_accounts
  • request_id: optional caller-supplied correlation id; echoed back in the response
  • cursor: optional opaque string from the previous page's next_cursor; empty or omitted returns the first page
  • limit: optional page size; clamped to 1..100, defaults to 20

Rules:

  • Requires an authenticated session.
  • Returns the available vault accounts, their latest performance data when present, and each account's creation_dt timestamp.
  • Strict JSON: unknown fields are rejected with invalid_get_vault_accounts.

Response (one vault_accounts event per request, then ack accepted):
