docs.title: user_deposit_address
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "user_deposit_address",
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "client_unix_ns": 1710000000000000000
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string user_deposit_address
  • subaccount_id: target trading subaccount id (uint64)
  • client_unix_ns: optional client timestamp in Unix nanoseconds; gateway receive time is used if omitted or zero

Rules:

  • Requires an authenticated wallet-bound session.
  • The wallet is the authenticated bound wallet. The request does not accept a wallet override.
  • The request does not include amount, token account, deposit address, transaction bytes, or VAA bytes.
  • This request registers the derived EVM deposit address for the authenticated wallet and subaccount. It does not transfer collateral or specify an amount.
  • The actual deposit amount is determined from the later EVM token transfer.
  • Send this command before transferring tokens. If a completed EVM transfer is delayed in reaching the trading account, it is safe to send the same request again and wait for another UserDepositAddressStatus.

UserDeposit address derivation:

  • wallet: the authenticated bound wallet as 32 bytes.
  • subaccount_id: uint64, encoded big-endian for the CREATE2 salt input.
  • evm_vault: deployed EVMVault address from GET /v1/evm/addresses field gateway.
  • userDepositInitCodeHash: keccak256(type(UserDeposit).creationCode), exposed on-chain as EVMVault.userDepositInitCodeHash() and returned by GET /v1/evm/addresses field user_deposit_init_code_hash.

Formula:

salt = keccak256(wallet || uint64_be(subaccount_id))
user_deposit_address = last20bytes(
  keccak256(0xff || evm_vault || salt || userDepositInitCodeHash)
)

Clients should fetch GET /v1/evm/addresses from the same gateway they use for WebSocket commands instead of hardcoding local deployment artifacts.

Completion:

  • A successful submission does not emit a generic ack accepted.
  • Wait for the matching UserDepositAddressStatus event. It confirms that the wallet/subaccount deposit address is registered.
  • Validation and forwarding failures still return ack rejected or ack busy.

Busy:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "busy", "reason": "sequencer_unreachable" }

Common rejects:

  • invalid_user_deposit_address
  • subaccount_id_required
  • auth_required
  • invalid_actor_pubkey

docs.title: Software-signed proof construction
docs.text:
Unless a command section states otherwise, a software-signed proof uses this Ed25519 message:

ascii(signature_domain) || 0x00 || unsigned_proof_bytes

unsigned_proof_bytes is the raw proof prefix and decoded command payload in the exact field order documented for that command. It excludes both signer_pubkey and signature. The transmitted raw proof is:

unsigned_proof_bytes || signer_pubkey[32] || signature[64]

All integer fields in these proofs are little-endian unless a command section explicitly says otherwise. Sign the domain bytes and the single NUL delimiter; the delimiter is part of the message. iat and exp in signed proofs are UTC Unix seconds.

docs.title: signed_create_vault
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_create_vault", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed create-vault proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_create_vault
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed create-vault proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 194 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_CREATE_VAULT_V1
  • The raw proof contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • source_subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • create_vault ContractCreateVaultV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractCreateVaultV1 fields:

  • vault_id uint32
  • reserved0 uint32
  • operation_subaccount_id uint64
  • requested_vault_collateral uint64
  • vault_creation_fee uint64
  • request_id64 uint64

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • Requires active wallet-bound authentication.
  • Sender in proof is the user wallet. signer_pubkey must match the authenticated session signer: wallet for wallet auth, delegate key for delegate auth.
  • Authenticated actor must have access to source_subaccount_id.
  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • source_subaccount_id may be 0
  • vault_id must be in 0..31
  • operation_subaccount_id must be > 0
  • operation_subaccount_id must differ from source_subaccount_id
  • requested_vault_collateral must be > 0
  • requested_vault_collateral + vault_creation_fee must not overflow uint64
  • exp must be > 0. The gateway admission deadline is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "create_vault": {
    "vault_id": 0,
    "reserved0": 0,
    "operation_subaccount_id": 1,
    "requested_vault_collateral": 1000000,
    "vault_creation_fee": 100000000,
    "request_id64": 9006
  }
}

CreateVault is emitted for non-approved create-vault decisions:

{
  "type": "CreateVault",
  "seq": 122,
  "client_instruction_id": "9006",
  "subaccount_id": 1,
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "source_subaccount_pubkey": "<source subaccount PDA>",
  "operation_subaccount_id": 1,
  "operation_subaccount_pubkey": "<operation subaccount PDA>",
  "vault_id": 0,
  "vault_account_pubkey": "<vault PDA>",
  "participant_account_pubkey": "<participant PDA>",
  "requested_vault_collateral": 1000000,
  "vault_creation_fee": 100000000,
  "total_debit": 101000000,
  "status": 1,
  "error_code": 0,
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 77
}
  • status=1 and error_code=0 means the vault already exists.
  • Other non-approved decisions are failures.
  • status and error_code are always present, including zero-valued fields.
  • vault_id is always present; 0 is a valid vault id.
  • Approved decisions are not forwarded as CreateVault; clients wait for CreateVaultStatus.

docs.title: signed_set_delegate
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_set_delegate", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed set-delegate proof bytes>" }

Raw software-signed proof definition:

  • Wire length: 160 bytes
  • Payload: owner_pubkey(32) || delegate_key(32) || delegate_nonce(8) || request_id64(8) || iat(8) || exp(8)
  • Signature: 64 bytes over the 96-byte payload. Signer is owner_pubkey.

Raw Ledger-signed proof definition:

  • Wire length: 277 bytes
  • Signed payload: 85-byte Solana off-chain V0 prefix || base64(payload96)
  • Signature: 64 bytes over the full signed payload
  • Ledger prefix signer must be owner_pubkey

Rules enforced:

  • Requires owner wallet authentication. Delegate-authenticated sessions are rejected.
  • owner_pubkey must match the authenticated wallet.
  • delegate_nonce must be greater than 0; on-chain validation requires it to be exactly the next user delegate nonce.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use and must be clear.
  • iat and exp must be greater than 0; gateway caps effective lifetime to 5 seconds for raw software proofs and 60 seconds for Ledger proofs.
  • On-chain validation requires iat <= exp and exp not to be expired at execution time.
  • Settlement emits SetDelegateStatus after the on-chain transaction reaches terminal status.

Authoritative result events arrive through the private/account stream.

SetDelegateStatus is emitted for terminal settlement status:

{
  "type": "SetDelegateStatus",
  "seq": 123,
  "client_instruction_id": "9006",
  "wallet": "<owner wallet>",
  "delegate_pubkey": "<delegate pubkey>",
  "delegate_nonce": 1,
  "status": 0,
  "error_code": 0,
  "term": 77
}
  • status=0 and error_code=0 means finalized success.
  • Nonzero status or nonzero error_code means settlement failed.
  • Known nonzero error_code values may include error_domain, error, and error_message when available.
  • status and error_code are always present, including zero-valued success fields.
  • Only terminal settlement statuses are delivered as private events.

docs.title: signed_order
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_order", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed order proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_order
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed order proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 191 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_ORDER_V1
  • The raw proof is not JSON. It contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • order ContractOrderV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractOrderV1 fields:

  • symbol uint32
  • price uint64
  • qty uint64
  • tif uint8
  • order_type uint8
  • execution_mode uint8
  • role uint8
  • delta_ppm int32
  • side uint8
  • request_id64 uint64

Allowed enum values:

  • tif: 0 = IOC, 1 = GTC
  • order_type: 0 = LIMIT, 1 = MARK_TO_MID, 2 = MARKET
  • execution_mode: 0 = NORMAL, 1 = MAINTENANCE_LIQUIDATION, 2 = ADL, 3 = VAULT_LIQUIDATION, 4 = REDUCE_ONLY
  • role: 0 = MAKER, 1 = TAKER
  • side: 0 = BUY, 1 = SELL

These enum values are the public signed-wire values.

Role-based command timing:

The sequencer's taker delay defaults to 300 ms; deployments can configure another delay. The rules below use that default.

  • Taker orders become eligible to enter an auction after 300 ms.
  • Maker orders are eligible for the next auction.
  • The same role-based timing applies to cancels and modifies. Maker cancels and maker modifies are eligible for the next auction; taker cancels and taker modifies become eligible after 300 ms.
  • The cancel/modify role must match the live order role, so a taker cannot bypass this timing by marking a command as maker.

docs.title: Price and quantity encoding
docs.text:
• price is a raw uint64 integer carried in wire format; the market's px_exponent is applied to interpret it as a decimal price.
  • Human price is price * 10^(px_exponent).
  • Example: if px_exponent = -2 and price = 10001, the human price is 100.01.
  • qty is a raw uint64 integer carried in wire format in units of 10^(-size_decimals) for that market.
  • Human quantity is qty * 10^(-size_decimals).
  • Risk View requires raw order quantity to fit a signed 64-bit integer: 1..9223372036854775807, despite the unsigned wire field.
  • To encode a human decimal quantity, clients compute raw_qty = human_qty * 10^(size_decimals).
  • A human decimal quantity is valid only if it is exactly representable at that market resolution and raw_qty > 0.
  • This means a client decimal input may have at most size_decimals fractional digits.
  • Examples:
  • BTC with size_decimals = 5: minimum increment is 0.00001; 10.12345 is valid and encodes as 1012345; 10.123456 is invalid because it is not exactly representable as uint64 qty
  • ETH with size_decimals = 4: minimum increment is 0.0001; 10.1234 is valid and encodes as 101234; 10.12345 is invalid because it is not exactly representable as uint64 qty

Limit-price acceptance rule:

  • The gateway validates the price field only for LIMIT orders.
  • The rule is based on 6 - size_decimals.
  • Starting from the scaled decimal price, trailing zeros are stripped first.
  • After stripping trailing zeros:
  • remaining decimal places must be <= 6 - size_decimals
  • if any decimal places remain, the normalized price must have at most 5 significant figures
  • Clients must apply this rule before submitting an order.

Equivalent intuition:

  • More size_decimals leaves fewer decimal places available for price.
  • When decimal places remain, prices are limited to 5 significant figures after normalization.

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • symbol must be active symbology and fit in uint32
  • qty must be > 0
  • For signed raw integer orders, representable quantity precision is implied by the wire encoding above; clients accepting human decimal qty input must reject values with more than size_decimals fractional digits
  • Public gateway clients may submit only execution_mode = 0 = NORMAL or execution_mode = 4 = REDUCE_ONLY. Modes 1, 2, and 3 are reserved for internal liquidation workflows.
  • role must be explicitly provided as MAKER or TAKER; gateway does not infer it from order_type or tif
  • LIMIT orders require price > 0
  • LIMIT orders require the raw price to satisfy the gateway's accepted price grid for that symbol (px_exponent, size_decimals, 6 - size_decimals, 5-significant-figure rule)
  • MARK_TO_MID orders allow negative, positive, or zero delta_ppm
  • MARK_TO_MID orders do not use the price field for gateway validation
  • MARK_TO_MID orders require a current mark price in gateway for precheck; the final executable limit is determined at auction time from Pyth
  • MARK_TO_MID orders accept the full signed 32-bit delta_ppm range; the matcher rejects only when the derived auction-time price is invalid or cannot be represented on the symbol price grid
  • MARKET orders require tif = IOC and role = TAKER
  • MARKET orders may use price as a reference price and positive delta_ppm as the maximum adverse slippage
  • MARKET orders with price = 0 require delta_ppm = 0; this 0/0 combination is an unrestricted market order
  • MARKET orders with price > 0 are protected market orders and require delta_ppm > 0
  • protected MARKET orders require delta_ppm <= 1000000, i.e. at most 100% adverse slippage
  • MARKET orders require delta_ppm >= 0; zero is valid only for the unrestricted price = 0, delta_ppm = 0 combination
  • exp must be > 0. The gateway admission deadline is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.
  • iat is the client send time in Unix seconds; the gateway converts it to nanoseconds for event timing fields.

Order lifetime after admission:

  • The gateway's five-second admission window does not shorten an admitted GTC order's signed exp. A GTC order can remain live until that expiry, unless filled or cancelled earlier.
  • Ordinary IOC orders have a matching deadline of the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. Unfilled quantity is cancelled after their eligible auction; the deadline does not give them repeated auctions.
  • A successful modify replaces the working GTC order's expiry with the modify proof's signed exp, even if price and quantity stay unchanged.

For example, a GTC order signed at 12:00 with exp at 13:00 must reach the gateway before 12:00:05, but it can remain live until 13:00.

Mark-to-mid price semantics:

  • For MARK_TO_MID, clients should treat price as ignored and usually send 0.
  • The gateway does not apply the LIMIT price-grid rule to MARK_TO_MID.
  • The executable limit is determined at auction time from the current Pyth mark and delta_ppm.
  • delta_ppm is parts per million of that auction-time mark price.
  • A zero delta_ppm derives the current mark price before matcher price-grid snapping.
  • The raw price delta is floor(mark_price * abs(delta_ppm) / 1_000_000), with a minimum of one raw price unit for nonzero delta_ppm.
  • Effective limit derivation:
  • buy: derived_limit = mark_price - raw_delta when delta_ppm > 0, and mark_price + raw_delta when delta_ppm < 0
  • sell: derived_limit = mark_price + raw_delta when delta_ppm > 0, and mark_price - raw_delta when delta_ppm < 0
  • Positive delta_ppm moves buys below mark and sells above mark.
  • Negative delta_ppm moves the raw derived buy above mark and the raw derived sell below mark.
  • The derived limit is snapped to the market price grid without worsening the owner price: buys snap down and sells snap up. A small negative delta may therefore snap back to the current grid level instead of crossing.
  • The symbol's explicit limit-price grid affects LIMIT orders directly, while MARK_TO_MID is governed by mark availability, delta_ppm, the validity of the derived price, and price-grid snapping.

Market-order slippage semantics:

  • For a protected MARKET order, price is the client-supplied reference price and delta_ppm is parts per million of that reference price.
  • The raw adverse-price allowance is floor(price * delta_ppm / 1_000_000).
  • A protected buy may execute at or below price + allowance.
  • A protected sell may execute at or above max(price - allowance, 0).
  • Prices farther in the favorable direction remain eligible; the protection is one-sided.
  • Eligibility is evaluated against the auction fill price. The reference price is not added as a clearing-price candidate.
  • The reference price and slippage are used unchanged, without applying the LIMIT price-grid rule to them.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "subaccount_id": 7,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "order": {
    "symbol": 7,
    "price": 5000000,
    "qty": 1000,
    "tif": 1,
    "order_type": 0,
    "execution_mode": 0,
    "role": 0,
    "delta_ppm": 0,
    "side": 0,
    "request_id64": 9001
  }
}

Example meanings:

  • Limit maker buy order: order_type=0, role=0, side=0, tif=1, price>0
  • Mark-to-mid taker buy below mark: order_type=1, role=1, side=0, delta_ppm>0
  • Mark-to-mid order at mark: order_type=1, delta_ppm=0
  • Mark-to-mid maker buy above mark: order_type=1, role=0, side=0, delta_ppm<0
  • Unrestricted market taker sell: order_type=2, role=1, side=1, tif=0, price=0, delta_ppm=0
  • Protected market taker buy with 1% adverse slippage: order_type=2, role=1, side=0, tif=0, price>0, delta_ppm=10000

Reduce-only order semantics:

  • Set execution_mode = 4 in the signed order proof; the JSON envelope remains signed_order with msg_b64, without a top-level reduce_only field.
  • Sells reduce a long position; buys reduce a short position in the same subaccount and symbol. At settlement, quantity is clipped to available reducing capacity, including zero while flat or on the wrong side. An exit cannot increase exposure or reverse the position.
  • A matched Fill is provisional. Reconcile a reduce-only FillSettled using settled_qty and applied_fee, including zero; reduced_qty is the quantity removed from the match. It is distinct from a failed-settlement bust.
  • A successful reduce-only close that exhausts a position invalidates TP/SL groups protecting that position direction. An unrelated normal close does not automatically cancel them. See TP/SL and reduce-only for quantity and manual-close examples.

docs.title: signed_cancel
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_cancel", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed cancel proof bytes>" }

docs.title: signed_modify
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_modify", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed modify proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_modify
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed modify proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 215 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_MODIFY_V1
  • The raw proof contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • modify ContractModifyV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractModifyV1 fields:

  • external_order_id uint64
  • request_id64 uint64
  • original_iat uint64
  • original_request_id64 uint64
  • symbol uint32
  • role uint8
  • side uint8
  • tif uint8
  • order_type uint8
  • execution_mode uint8
  • price uint64
  • qty uint64
  • delta_ppm int32

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • external_order_id must be > 0
  • original_iat must be > 0
  • top-level modify iat must not be earlier than original_iat
  • original_request_id64 must be > 0 and must leave bit 63 clear
  • qty must be > 0
  • symbol must be active symbology
  • role must be 0 = MAKER or 1 = TAKER
  • side, tif, and order_type must be valid enum values
  • Public gateway clients may submit only execution_mode = 0 = NORMAL or execution_mode = 4 = REDUCE_ONLY. Modes 1, 2, and 3 are reserved for internal liquidation workflows.
  • exp must be > 0. The gateway admission deadline is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Execution rules:

  • The target order must exist and still be live.
  • The target order must not be IOC or MARKET.
  • The modify role must match the original order role.
  • The modify side, tif, and order_type must match the original order.
  • The modify execution_mode must match the original order.
  • The modify original_iat and original_request_id64 must match the original live order's signed order proof identity.
  • The modify qty must be <= the target order's current live remaining quantity. Modify can reduce or keep size unchanged, but cannot increase size. To increase size, cancel the existing order and submit a new order after the cancel is acknowledged.
  • A successful modify updates price, qty, delta_ppm, and the working order's expiry from the modify proof's signed exp.
  • Maker modifies are eligible for the next auction.
  • Taker modifies become eligible to enter an auction after 300 ms.
  • The role must match the live order, so a taker cannot bypass this timing by marking a modify as maker.
  • MARK_TO_MID modifies use an executable price determined at auction time from the current Pyth mark and requested delta_ppm; invalid derived prices are rejected.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "subaccount_id": 7,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "modify": {
    "external_order_id": 123456,
    "request_id64": 9005,
    "original_iat": 1710000000,
    "original_request_id64": 9001,
    "symbol": 7,
    "role": 0,
    "side": 0,
    "tif": 1,

docs.title: signed_conditional_group
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_conditional_group", "version": 1, "msg_b64": "<base64 signed conditional-group proof bytes>" }

The proof is 196 bytes and uses signature domain AETHEON_COND_V1. Its envelope contains, in order, the sender [32]byte, partition uint16, subaccount uint64, iat uint64, exp uint64, the 42-byte conditional group, signer [32]byte, and signature [64]byte. Integers are little-endian with no padding; iat and exp are Unix seconds. The JSON envelope version is required and must be 1.

Conditional group fields, in wire order:

  • symbol uint32
  • qty uint64
  • exit_side uint8: 0 = BUY, 1 = SELL
  • leg_flags uint8: bit 1 = take profit, bit 2 = stop loss
  • tp_trigger_sources and sl_trigger_sources uint8: bit 1 = oracle, bit 2 = auction; sources may be combined
  • version uint8: must be 1
  • activation_mode uint8: 0 = parent_fill, 1 = immediate
  • tp_trigger_price and sl_trigger_price uint64; a take-profit child uses its trigger price as its limit price
  • request_id64 uint64

Rules enforced by the gateway and Risk View:

  • At least one conditional leg is enabled and qty is between 1 and 9223372036854775807 inclusive.
  • Enabled trigger prices must lie on the market price grid; disabled leg fields must be zero.
  • When both legs are enabled, stop loss must be below take profit for a sell exit. The comparison is reversed for a buy exit.
  • The take-profit child limit is derived from its trigger price.
  • In parent_fill mode, bind a subsequently submitted normal parent with the same wallet, symbol, and subaccount, quantity at least the group's signed qty, and the opposite side. Protection grows from successfully settled parent fills up to the group's signed qty, not the full net position or unrelated fills. Residual exposure can rearm after child settlement; later settled parent fills can add protection.
  • In immediate mode, no parent is submitted. The subaccount must have a position reduced by exit_side. The group starts with submitted qty, which is not automatically resized by unrelated trades.
  • Both activation modes can rearm residual protected quantity after the selected child and its pending settlements are resolved.
  • A successful parent modification invalidates its TP/SL group. A child already active or being activated remains a live ordinary order, is not rearmed by Bop, and is the trader's responsibility to monitor or cancel.
  • exp is required and may be at most 90 days after gateway admission.

Take-profit legs become TAKER, REDUCE_ONLY GTC limit orders at the TP trigger price. Stop-loss legs become TAKER, REDUCE_ONLY unrestricted market IOC orders with price = 0 and delta_ppm = 0; the SL trigger is not an execution-price guarantee. The group and each enabled leg receive distinct external order IDs. Conditional groups are immutable; cancel and replace a group to change it.

See TP/SL and reduce-only for trigger directions, activation flows, exit sizing, and cancellation behavior after manual trades.

docs.title: signed_conditional_parent
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "signed_conditional_parent",
  "version": 1,
  "conditional_group_external_order_id": "101",
  "msg_b64": "<base64 signed order proof bytes>"
}

This command binds a normal signed order to a previously approved parent_fill group; it cannot bind an immediate group. msg_b64 uses the same order proof and AETHEON_ORDER_V1 signature domain as signed_order. The JSON envelope version is required and must be 1; conditional_group_external_order_id is the ID received in ConditionalApproved. Send this backend-assigned ID back as a decimal string to identify the group to bind to the parent. JSON numbers are rejected for this request field.

Submit the parent only after receiving ConditionalApproved. Bop verifies that the parent has the same wallet, subaccount, and symbol as the group, has quantity at least the group's signed qty, and has the opposite side from the conditional exit. Risk then evaluates the parent as a normal new order. OrderAccepted or OrderReject is the authoritative parent result. For a group in waiting_parent, a binding mismatch, such as a smaller quantity, rejects the attempted parent with ConditionalInvalidGroup while leaving the group in waiting_parent; submit an eligible parent or cancel the unused group. If a successfully bound parent is rejected with no settled or pending fills, Bop completes the unprotected group with ConditionalCompleted; wait for that event to confirm completion. A timeout or disconnect is ambiguous, so the client must wait for the account stream or reconnect and use its snapshot rather than guessing whether the parent was accepted.

docs.title: signed_conditional_cancel
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_conditional_cancel", "version": 1, "msg_b64": "<base64 signed cancel proof bytes>" }

This command uses the existing AETHEON_CANCEL_V2 proof format. Set external_order_id to the conditional group ID, not a take-profit or stop-loss leg ID. The JSON envelope version is required and must be 1.

Group cancellation applies while waiting for a parent or settled fill, or while dormant. It can be rejected once activation starts. Cancel an accepted active child with signed_cancel using ConditionalTriggered.selected_external_order_id; successful user child cancellation terminates the bracket without rearming residual exposure.

docs.title: signed_withdraw
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_withdraw", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed withdraw proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_withdraw
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed withdraw proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Software-signed wire length: 234 bytes
  • Software signature domain: AETHEON_WITHDRAW_V1
  • Ledger V0 wire length: 333 bytes
  • Ledger V0 body: canonical base64 of the compact withdraw payload.
  • The compact withdraw payload contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • withdraw ContractWithdrawV1
  • Software proof appends signer_pubkey [32]byte and signature [64]byte.
  • Ledger proof is ledger_signed_payload || signature, where the signer pubkey is in the Ledger prefix.

Decoded ContractWithdrawV1 fields:

  • amount uint64
  • owner_wallet [32]byte
  • dest_token_account [32]byte; for EVM withdraw this is a bytes32 EVM address word: 12 leading zero bytes followed by the 20-byte EVM recipient address.
  • request_id64 uint64

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • amount must be > 0
  • exp must be > 0. The gateway admission deadline is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds for software proofs, or iat + 60 seconds for Ledger proofs. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "subaccount_id": 7,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "withdraw": {
    "amount": 1000000,
    "owner_wallet": "<32-byte wallet pubkey bytes>",
    "dest_token_account": "<bytes32 EVM address word>",
    "request_id64": 9004
  }
}

Withdraw destination policy:

  • dest_token_account must encode the target EVM recipient as 0x000000000000000000000000<20-byte address>.
  • Settlement transfers collateral asynchronously to the target EVM recipient.

docs.title: signed_deposit_vault
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_deposit_vault", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed deposit-vault proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_deposit_vault
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed deposit-vault proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 202 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_DEPOSIT_VAULT_V1
  • The raw proof contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • source_subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • deposit_vault ContractDepositVaultV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractDepositVaultV1 fields:

  • vault_account_pubkey [32]byte
  • deposit_amount uint64
  • request_id64 uint64

DepositVaultStatus additionally reports settlement accounting fields:

  • deposit_amount: requested source debit amount.
  • insurance_payback: amount used to repay owe_to_insurance on the vault operation subaccount before vault credit.
  • actual_deposit: amount actually credited to the vault operation subaccount and used for share/cost-basis accounting.

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • Requires active wallet-bound authentication.
  • Sender in proof is the user wallet. signer_pubkey must match the authenticated session signer: wallet for wallet auth, delegate key for delegate auth.
  • Authenticated actor must have access to source_subaccount_id.
  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • deposit_amount must be > 0
  • exp must be > 0. The gateway admission deadline is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "deposit_vault": {
    "vault_account_pubkey": "<32-byte vault PDA>",
    "deposit_amount": 1000000,
    "request_id64": 9007
  }
}

docs.title: signed_transfer_subaccount
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_transfer_subaccount", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed transfer-subaccount proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_transfer_subaccount
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed transfer-subaccount proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 178 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_TRANSFER_SUBACCOUNT_V1
  • The raw proof contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • source_subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • transfer_subaccount ContractTransferSubaccountV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractTransferSubaccountV1 fields:

  • target_subaccount_id uint64
  • amount uint64
  • request_id64 uint64

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • Requires active wallet-bound authentication.
  • Sender in proof is the user wallet. signer_pubkey must match the authenticated session signer: wallet for wallet auth, delegate key for delegate auth.
  • Authenticated actor must have access to source_subaccount_id.
  • target_subaccount_id must differ from source_subaccount_id. If the target subaccount does not exist, settlement creates it for the same user.
  • request_id64 must be > 0; it is passed through unchanged and may be a nonce, sequence number, or trace ID.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • amount must be > 0
  • exp must be > 0. The gateway admission deadline is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "transfer_subaccount": {
    "target_subaccount_id": 2,
    "amount": 1000000,
    "request_id64": 9009
  }
}

TransferSubaccountStatus is emitted after settlement status:

{
  "type": "TransferSubaccountStatus",
  "seq": 12346,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "client_instruction_id": "9009",
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "source_subaccount_pubkey": "<source subaccount PDA>",
  "target_subaccount_id": 2,
  "target_subaccount_pubkey": "<target subaccount PDA>",
  "transfer_amount": 1000000,
  "insurance_payback": 0,
  "status": 0,
  "error_code": 0,
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 2
}

Signed submit rules:

  • Type-driven parse/validation (signed_order uses order parser, signed_create_vault uses create-vault parser, etc.).
  • Sender in proof is the user wallet. signer_pubkey must match the authenticated session signer: wallet for wallet auth, delegate key for delegate auth.
  • Client must already be authenticated and wallet-bound.
  • Signed submit never emits auth challenge; unauthenticated submit is rejected.
  • Delegate rules are enforced based on auth mode and delegate binding validity.
  • The public WebSocket API does not expose a signed_deposit command. User collateral deposits use user_deposit_address plus the EVM deposit flow.

Signed submit responses:

  • Successful submit does not emit an immediate acceptance receipt.
  • Authoritative order/cancel/modify/conditional/collateral/liquidation/vault/transfer state changes arrive through private/account stream events such as OrderAccepted, ConditionalApproved, ConditionalTriggered, ConditionalExpired, ConditionalCancelled, ConditionalInvalidated, ConditionalCompleted, OrderReject, CancelAck, CancelReject, ModifyAck, ModifyReject, UserDepositAddressStatus, UserCollateralUpdate, AccountFundingUpdate, LiquidationTriggered, LiquidationCleared, WithdrawStatus, CreateVaultStatus, CreateVault, DepositVaultStatus, DepositVault, WithdrawVaultStatus, WithdrawVault, VaultOperationSubaccountCollateralChange, TransferSubaccountStatus, and SetDelegateStatus.
  • Local validation and submit transport failures still return ack with rejected or busy:
{
  "type": "ack",
  "status": "rejected",
  "reason": "invalid_symbol",
  "client_instruction_id": "123"
}

or

{
  "type": "ack",
  "status": "busy",
  "reason": "sequencer_unreachable",
  "client_instruction_id": "123"
}

docs.title: ping
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "ping", "client_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000 }

Fields:

  • type: literal string ping
  • client_unix_ns: required integer timestamp supplied by the client.
  • No other request fields are accepted.

Success:

{ "type": "pong", "client_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000 }

RTT usage:

  • The gateway echoes client_unix_ns unchanged.
  • The client should capture a local timestamp immediately before send and another local timestamp when the pong is received.
  • A simple RTT estimate is client_recv_unix_ns - pong.client_unix_ns.
  • This measures application-layer round-trip time from the client clock domain. It does not measure one-way client->gateway latency.
  • The gateway does not provide a server timestamp for RTT calculation because that would mix clock domains and be sensitive to clock drift.

docs.title: Flow A: wallet direct signing (no delegate)
docs.text:
1. auth_wallet with wallet_pubkey + expiry_seconds.
  2. Receive auth_challenge.
  3. Sign challenge, send auth_response, and wait for ack accepted.
  4. Send subscribe_account and wait for AccountSnapshot before submitting trading commands.
  5. Before transferring EVM deposit tokens, send user_deposit_address and wait for the matching UserDepositAddressStatus so the wallet/subaccount EVM deposit address is registered.
  6. Transfer collateral to that address, then wait for UserCollateralUpdate before treating the trading subaccount as funded.
  7. Send signed_order / signed_cancel / signed_modify / signed_conditional_group / signed_conditional_parent / signed_conditional_cancel / signed_withdraw / signed_create_vault / signed_deposit_vault / signed_withdraw_vault / signed_transfer_subaccount.

docs.title: Funding Accounts
docs.text:
A Superluminal account is identified by a Fogo Ed25519 wallet. Testnet collateral is provisioned by Superluminal. Manual EVM deposits are credited to a numbered trading subaccount after settlement on Fogo.

The Fogo wallet and the EVM wallet have different roles:

  • The Fogo wallet authenticates the Superluminal account and selects the trading subaccount.
  • The EVM wallet sends collateral and pays EVM gas for manual deposits. It does not need to have the same address or private key as the Fogo wallet.

Never send a manual deposit until Superluminal has confirmed that the derived deposit address is registered.

docs.title: Keypair format
docs.text:
The utilities accept a Solana-format Ed25519 keypair JSON file: a JSON array of 64 byte values. This is also the format produced by solana-keygen.

Protect the file as a private key. The utilities load it locally and use it only to sign the WebSocket authentication challenge; the private key is never sent to Superluminal.

docs.title: Install the deposit-address utility
docs.text:
The C++ and Python client bundles include a cross-platform deposit-address utility under funding-tools. It runs with Bun on Linux, macOS, and Windows; no prebuilt executable is distributed.

Requirements:

  • a supplied C++ or Python client bundle;
  • Bun 1.3.14 or newer; and
  • an existing Fogo keypair JSON file.

Install runtime dependencies once from the bundle's funding-tools directory:

cd funding-tools
bun install --production --frozen-lockfile

docs.title: Request testnet collateral
docs.text:
Ask the Superluminal team for testnet funds through the channel used to onboard you. Provide your public Fogo wallet address and intended subaccount ID; never send your keypair or private key. If the team asks for a registered EVM deposit address, prepare it with deposit:address below and provide the printed address.

After the team confirms funding, connect the trading client with the same wallet and subaccount. Wait for UserCollateralUpdate or a fresh AccountSnapshot showing the credited collateral before placing an order. An EVM transaction receipt alone does not prove that the trading balance was credited.

docs.title: Derive an address for a manual deposit
docs.text:
Use deposit:address when Superluminal asks for a registered address or for a manual ERC20 deposit. This command registers the Fogo wallet and subaccount, derives the corresponding EVM destination, and prints the authoritative EVM network and collateral token. It does not request an EVM private key or transfer funds.

bun run deposit:address \
  --keypair /path/to/fogo-wallet.json \
  --gateway https://gateway.example \
  --evm-rpc https://evm-rpc.example \
  --partition-id <u16> \
  --subaccount <u64>

Use the gateway origin, EVM RPC, and partition ID supplied for the same deployment. The gateway accepts subaccount IDs 0..31. Successful output has this form:

Fogo account:        <base58 wallet address>
Subaccount:          <subaccount id>
EVM chain ID:        <decimal chain id>
Collateral token:    <0x ERC20 address>
EVM deposit address: <0x deposit address>
Deposit address ready.
Transfer only the listed collateral token on the listed EVM chain.

After Deposit address ready.:

  1. Configure the EVM wallet for the printed chain.
  2. Connect a trading client with the same Fogo wallet and subaccount.
  3. Transfer only the printed collateral token to the printed deposit address.
  4. Observe its account stream and wait for UserCollateralUpdate before treating the trading account as funded.

The address utility exits after registration; it does not need to remain open while the EVM transfer settles.

An EVM receipt proves that the transfer was submitted; it does not prove that the trading balance was credited. Sending on another chain or sending another token will not fund the account.

docs.title: How the deposit address is derived
docs.text:
The deposit address is deterministic for a Fogo wallet and subaccount:

salt = keccak256(fogo_wallet_bytes || uint64_be(subaccount_id))

deposit_address = last20bytes(
  keccak256(0xff || evm_vault || salt || user_deposit_init_code_hash)
)

Inputs:

  • fogo_wallet_bytes: the authenticated 32-byte Ed25519 public key;
  • subaccount_id: the unsigned 64-bit subaccount number, encoded big-endian;
  • evm_vault: the gateway field from GET /v1/evm/addresses; and
  • user_deposit_init_code_hash: the matching field from that response.

Fetch those values from the same HTTP origin used for the WebSocket connection. Do not hardcode deployment addresses.

Before transferring collateral, authenticate the Fogo wallet and send:

{
  "type": "user_deposit_address",
  "subaccount_id": 0
}

Wait for the matching UserDepositAddressStatus. Registration success does not emit a generic ack accepted; validation or forwarding failures emit ack rejected or ack busy.

See user_deposit_address for the full wire contract.

docs.title: TP/SL and Reduce-only
docs.text: Take-profit (TP) and stop-loss (SL) groups create conditional exits from a symbol's net position in one trading subaccount. Each group has a quantity; it does not automatically resize to cover the entire position as other orders trade. Exits are reduce-only: they cannot increase exposure or reverse the position at settlement.

docs.title: Choose an activation mode
docs.text:
Mode When protection starts Exit quantity parent_fill (0 on the signed wire) After a bound parent fill settles successfully Settled parent fills, capped at signed group qty, less successfully settled exits immediate (1 on the signed wire) On approval, without a parent order Submitted qty, limited by the remaining position at settlement

For immediate, the subaccount must already have a position that the exit side reduces. The web trading application's Protect position action defaults to the full position size displayed at submission and accepts a smaller TP/SL quantity. Later unrelated fills do not resize that group. The web order form also accepts a TP/SL quantity in base units for a new parent order; leaving it blank uses the full parent quantity. TP alone, SL alone, or both can be submitted. A position may have multiple independently sized groups, each cancelled separately. Reduce-only settlement prevents their combined exits from reversing the position.

For parent_fill, the parent must match the group's wallet, subaccount, and symbol, have at least the group's quantity, and have the opposite side. Protection grows only from that parent's successfully settled fills, capped at the signed group quantity. Parent fills beyond that cap are unprotected by this group. Existing exposure and fills from other orders are not added to the group's quantity. A provisional or busted parent fill does not add protection.

docs.title: Example: existing exposure plus a parent order
docs.text:
You are long 2 units and submit a buy parent for 1 with TP/SL. After it fills and settles, you are long 3, but that group has an exit quantity of 1. If its exit fully settles, you remain long 2. The exit reduces the net position; there is no separately identified lot being closed.

To protect all 3 units, cancel the existing dormant group, wait for its cancellation, and submit an immediate group with qty corresponding to 3. Read the current account state before choosing that quantity.

docs.title: Submit TP/SL
docs.text:
Authenticate, subscribe to the account stream, and use current symbology to encode prices and quantities. The conditional-group reference defines the 196-byte signed proof, including its activation_mode byte. Enable TP, SL, or both. Disabled leg fields must be zero.

For an existing position:

  1. Choose the opposite exit side: SELL for a long, BUY for a short.
  2. Sign a group with activation_mode = 1, the exit quantity, trigger prices, trigger sources, and expiry.
  3. Send signed_conditional_group with JSON envelope version: 1.
  4. Wait for ConditionalApproved. Do not submit a parent.

For activation by a new parent order:

  1. Sign and submit the group with activation_mode = 0.
  2. Wait for ConditionalApproved and retain its group_external_order_id.
  3. Send signed_conditional_parent using that group ID and a normal order proof with quantity at least the group's.
  4. Observe the parent's OrderAccepted or OrderReject, then settlement. Triggers become eligible only after a successful parent settlement.

A rejected binding does not cancel the group. For example, a parent quantity of 1 cannot bind to a group signed for 2; the group stays in waiting_parent. Submit an eligible parent or cancel that unused group. Rejection after successful binding instead completes an unprotected group with ConditionalCompleted.

A disconnect or timeout does not establish whether a submission succeeded. Reconnect and reconcile the account snapshot and lifecycle events.

docs.title: Trigger prices and exit orders
docs.text:
Trigger sources are a bit mask: 1 = oracle, 2 = completed-auction fill price, 3 = either. A selected source triggers when its observed price reaches or passes the threshold:

Position Exit side TP triggers SL triggers Long SELL Price >= TP price Price <= SL price Short BUY Price <= TP price Price >= SL price

When both legs are enabled, SL must be below TP for a long position and above TP for a short position. Prices must satisfy the market price grid. The latest cached price is also evaluated when settled parent exposure becomes protected or residual exposure rearms.

The selected leg becomes a TAKER, REDUCE_ONLY order:

  • TP becomes a GTC limit order whose limit is the TP trigger price.
  • SL becomes an unrestricted market IOC order (price = 0, delta_ppm = 0). The trigger price is not a guaranteed execution price or a slippage bound.

A TP child carries the group's signed expiry. An SL child has a matching deadline of the earlier of the group expiry and five seconds after activation; its unfilled remainder is cancelled after its eligible auction.

When a leg triggers, its sibling is removed from trigger storage and emits a CancelAck. ConditionalTriggered.selected_external_order_id supplies the new active child ID, replacing the selected dormant leg ID. Use that ID for the child's ordinary OrderAccepted, fills, settlements, and cancellation. This applies on the first trigger and every later trigger. A trigger does not guarantee order admission or execution.

After reconnecting, a snapshot group's pending_leg, when set to 1 = TP or 2 = SL, identifies the selected leg; that leg's external order ID is the active child ID. Reconcile working orders and lifecycle events to determine whether it is still live. Order history can associate children with their group through conditional_group_external_order_id and conditional_leg when available.

docs.title: Rearming remaining protection
docs.text:
Rearming restores conditional triggers after the active child has no remaining order quantity and all its matched fills have resolved. Both activation modes can rearm if protected quantity remains and the group has not been cancelled, invalidated, or expired. Failed child settlement does not consume protection. In parent_fill mode, parent fills settling while the child is active can also leave quantity for another cycle.

For example, a buy parent for 2 units settles 1 and its TP child activates for 1. The second parent unit settles while that child is active. Once the child fully matches and successfully settles its 1 unit, the group can rearm for the remaining 1.

A partially matched TP remains a live GTC limit order; it does not create a second child while its remainder is live. If an SL matches only part of its quantity, cancellation of the unfilled IOC remainder terminates the group with ConditionalCancelled, after pending fills resolve. It does not rearm that cancelled remainder.

Rearming emits ConditionalApproved. A parent-fill group with no protected quantity can instead wait for further parent fills in waiting_fill state. The next ConditionalTriggered supplies the new active child ID. Approval and snapshot qty fields retain the original signed group quantity; they do not report current remaining protection. The active child's OrderAccepted reports the quantity submitted for that trigger.

docs.title: Manual trades and closing the position
docs.text:
Unrelated normal trades do not resize or cancel a TP/SL group. Continuing the long-3 example above, a manual sell of 1 leaves you long 2 with the same 1-unit group. A later fully settled TP/SL exit leaves you long 1.

Alternatively, closing the full long-3 position behaves differently according to the manual order's mode:

Manual close TP/SL behavior after successful settlement makes the position flat Reduce-only sell 3 Groups protecting that subaccount, symbol, and position direction are invalidated; active children are cancelled as part of resolution Normal sell 3 The unrelated trade does not automatically cancel the groups; they can remain armed

The web trading application's Close position action uses a reduce-only market IOC order. A partial reduce-only close that leaves exposure does not automatically resize unrelated groups.

While flat, a remaining TP/SL exit cannot settle a new short position. If you open another long before the old group triggers or expires, that exit can reduce the new position. Explicitly cancel unwanted groups after a normal manual close, and confirm their lifecycle events before reusing the position.

docs.title: Change or cancel protection
docs.text:
Groups are immutable. Cancel and replace a group to change its quantity, trigger prices, sources, or expiry.

  • Before activation, send signed_conditional_cancel with the group ID and wait for ConditionalCancelled.
  • After activation, cancel the live child with signed_cancel using the ID from ConditionalTriggered.selected_external_order_id. A successful user child cancellation terminates the bracket and prevents residual exposure from rearming. A group cancel can be rejected while activation is in progress.
  • Cancelling a parent stops new fills. Successfully settled fills retain protection; pending fills are resolved through settlement. If no protected quantity or pending fills remain, the group completes.
  • A successful parent modification invalidates its group. An already active child remains an ordinary live order that the trader must monitor or cancel.

Group expiry is at most 90 days after gateway admission. Dormant expiry emits ConditionalExpired; an active child's rejection or expiry terminates its group. Use account lifecycle events and reconnect snapshots to reconcile state, rather than inferring group state from individual leg cancellations.

docs.title: Submit and reconcile reduce-only orders
docs.text:
Set execution_mode = 4 inside the signed ContractOrderV1 proof, then send the usual signed_order envelope. There is no top-level reduce_only request field. A modify must preserve the live order's execution mode; cancel and replace to change between normal and reduce-only.

Reduce-only sells can settle only against a long position; buys can settle only against a short. Settlement clips a provisional match to the available reducing capacity of each reduce-only side, including zero while flat or when the position has the wrong direction. It never expands the submitted quantity.

For example, if a provisional sell matches 2 units but the long position is only 1 at settlement, FillSettled reports qty = 2, settled_qty = 1, and reduced_qty = 1. The resulting position is flat. Fees are scaled to the settled quantity and reported in applied_fee.

For these settlement events, reconcile positions and fees using settled_qty and applied_fee. qty and fee retain the provisional match and requested fee. qty = settled_qty + reduced_qty; reduced quantity is distinct from a failed-settlement FillBusted. The reduce_only_leg, limiting_leg, and exhausted_leg booleans describe this account's side of the settlement.

docs.title: Reference-client support
docs.text: The C++ reference TUI supports immediate and parent-fill TP/SL, cancellation of existing groups or triggered children, and reduce-only order submission. See its usage guide. The Python reference TUI also supports these actions; see its usage guide. See the API reference for the signed command formats.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: The supported path to a first Superluminal testnet trade is to use one of the tested reference-client bundles. Each bundle contains its client source, this generated documentation site, conformance vectors, and a deposit-address utility.

docs.title: Choose a client
docs.text:
• C++ reference client: build the terminal client from source.
  • Python reference client: install and run the terminal client.

When reading this page on the hosted documentation site, download the current bundle and its manifest:

  • C++ reference client bundle
  • Python reference client bundle
  • Release manifest: source commit, version, build time, and SHA-256 checksums.

Verify the downloaded file against manifest.json before unpacking it. If this page is inside an extracted bundle, use the enclosing reference client and its adjacent funding-tools/ directory; do not look for another download inside the bundle. Use conformance/test-vectors.json to verify signing and lossless unsigned 64-bit decoding.

docs.title: First testnet trade
docs.text:
1. Download and verify one client bundle.
  2. Generate a new Solana-format Ed25519 keypair. Never use a bundled or shared key.
  3. Follow Funding accounts to request testnet collateral from Superluminal.
  4. Follow the selected C++ or Python guide to connect the same wallet and subaccount 0.
  5. Wait for AccountSnapshot, confirm credited collateral, and synchronize market data.
  6. Submit a small, explicitly price-bounded LIMIT or IOC order using current symbology.
  7. Observe OrderAccepted or OrderReject and any fill settlement events.
  8. Cancel a working order, reconnect, and reconcile account state.

The public gateway permits one authenticated WebSocket session per wallet. If asked to register a deposit address, run the deposit-address utility before the trading client; a second authenticated session preempts the first.

docs.title: Build a custom client
docs.text: The bundles are the executable examples and signing implementations. Use the public API reference for the underlying HTTP, WebSocket, and wire contracts when building an independent integration.

docs.title: Getting Started with the C++ Reference Client
docs.text:
The reference api_client is a C++20 terminal application for connecting to Superluminal, viewing native maker and taker books, monitoring a trading account, and submitting, modifying, and cancelling signed orders.

It is a reference application rather than a complete binding for every public API command. See the public API reference when building a custom integration.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
You need:

  • the C++ reference client bundle (from the hosted documentation, unless this page is already inside that bundle);
  • a C++20 compiler;
  • Meson and Ninja;
  • pkg-config, OpenSSL, and libsodium; and
  • a Solana-format Ed25519 keypair JSON file for your Fogo wallet.

On Ubuntu or Debian:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y \
  build-essential \
  libssl-dev \
  libsodium-dev \
  meson \
  ninja-build \
  pkg-config

The source bundle vendors FTXUI, IXWebSocket, and simdjson.

Before unpacking a hosted download, verify its checksum against the release manifest. If this page is inside an extracted bundle, continue with that enclosing bundle.

docs.title: Build the client
docs.text:
From the root of the standalone C++ source bundle:

meson setup build
meson compile -C build

The executable is written to:

build/api_client/api_client

Confirm the binary before connecting:

./build/api_client/api_client --version

docs.title: Fund the wallet
docs.text:
Request testnet collateral from Superluminal through your onboarding channel. Provide your public Fogo wallet address and intended subaccount, never your keypair. If asked to register an EVM deposit address, run the bundle's deposit:address command from funding-tools before starting the client. Its authenticated session would otherwise preempt the client's session.

See Funding accounts for the request, deposit-address, and balance-verification steps.

docs.title: Start the client
docs.text:
./build/api_client/api_client \
  --ws wss://testnet.slx.fi/ws \
  --keypair ./wallet.json \
  --subaccount_id 0 \
  --partition_id 0x01

Arguments:

  • --ws: WebSocket endpoint; both ws:// and wss:// are supported.
  • --keypair: Fogo wallet keypair JSON file.
  • --subaccount_id: trading subaccount displayed by the application.
  • --partition_id: signed-message partition; public testnet uses 0x01.
  • --feed_ids: optional comma-separated market IDs. When omitted, the client subscribes to every active market in the WebSocket SymbologySnapshot.

The client reads symbology and exchange config from the gateway WebSocket, then authenticates the wallet and starts the account and market subscriptions.

docs.title: Connection flow
docs.text:
The client performs these steps automatically:

  1. Read the initial SymbologySnapshot and ExchangeConfigSnapshot.
  2. Send auth_wallet with the wallet public key.
  3. Sign the returned auth_challenge locally.
  4. Send auth_response and wait for ack accepted.
  5. Send subscribe_account.
  6. Request the newest account order-history page.
  7. Subscribe to the selected active markets.

The first private account message is normally AccountSnapshot. Later account messages report accepted orders, rejects, fills, settlements, collateral, funding, modifications, and cancellations.

docs.title: Market data
docs.text:
Native subscribe_market streams contain two book views:

  • bookType: "maker"
  • bookType: "taker"

The client synchronizes them independently and combines them in its ladder. It also consumes Trade events. If it receives stream_reset, it discards the affected local book and resubscribes.

Use the API's book recovery rules for cursor continuity and absolute level updates, and account recovery rules for snapshot boundaries, settlement, and command reconciliation after disconnects.

Market IDs and integer scaling are deployment data. Read them from the initial WebSocket snapshot rather than hardcoding them.

Use px_exponent, tick_size, and size_decimals when converting human prices and quantities to raw wire integers.

Collateral, fees, PnL, and funding amounts use a separate fixed six-decimal USD scale; see Numeric units.

docs.title: Submit an order
docs.text:
The order ticket creates and signs a signed_order proof locally. Choose:

  • market;
  • buy or sell;
  • quantity;
  • GTC limit, GTC mark-to-mid, or IOC market order; and
  • explicit MAKER or TAKER role; and
  • Normal or Reduce only execution.

Role is not inferred. Market orders require TAKER. For a protected market order, provide a reference price and slippage from 1 to 1,000,000 ppm. Leave both fields empty for an unrestricted market order.

Sending the command successfully is not the final order result. Observe the private account stream:

  • ack rejected or ack busy reports a local command failure;
  • OrderAccepted confirms admission to the account stream;
  • OrderReject reports an asynchronous rejection; and
  • Fill, FillSettled, and FillBusted report execution and settlement.

Reduce only sets execution_mode = 4 in the signed order. Such an order can only reduce an existing position; the settled amount can be smaller than its provisional fill. The account view reconciles settled_qty and applied_fee.

docs.title: Submit or cancel TP/SL
docs.text:
The TP/SL section uses the ticket's selected market, exit side, and quantity. Enter a take-profit price, stop-loss price, or both. Leave a leg blank to disable it. Trigger prices must be on the market grid. The reference client selects both oracle and auction trigger sources and a 30-day expiry.

Choose Immediate to protect an existing position. Choose Parent fill to protect settled fills from a new parent order. For parent mode, first select the exit side and press Create TP/SL. Wait for ConditionalApproved and copy its group ID from the account panel. Enter that ID in Group ID, set the ordinary order ticket to the opposite side with the same market and a quantity at least as large as the group's, then press Submit Parent. The client signs and binds that order to the approved group; OrderAccepted or OrderReject gives its result. Settled parent fills protect at most the group's quantity; any larger remainder is unprotected by that group.

To cancel an existing group, enter its ID and press Cancel TP/SL. While the group is dormant or waiting, this sends signed_conditional_cancel. Once a leg triggers and its child is accepted as a working order, cancellation targets that child with signed_cancel. If the child ID is unavailable after reconnect, cancel it from Working Orders when it appears. Confirm cancellation with the private account stream; sending the request alone does not prove it succeeded. See TP/SL and reduce-only for lifecycle and sizing rules.

docs.title: Modify or cancel an order
docs.text:
Select a working order in the TUI to modify or cancel it. The client signs the corresponding command and waits for ModifyAck, ModifyReject, CancelAck, or CancelReject on the account stream.

The client preserves the execution mode from both OrderAccepted and AccountSnapshot, so a reduce-only order can be modified after reconnect.

docs.title: First-run checklist
docs.text:
1. Check https://testnet.slx.fi/healthz returns ok.
  2. Connect to the WebSocket and confirm its snapshot contains an active market.
  3. Request testnet collateral from Superluminal.
  4. Start api_client with the same keypair and subaccount 0.
  5. Confirm credited collateral in AccountSnapshot and synchronize market data.
  6. Submit a small order and observe its private lifecycle events.
  7. Cancel it if it remains working.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
• Session preempted: another connection authenticated the same wallet.
  • Invalid symbol: reconnect and use an active market ID from the snapshot.
  • Invalid price grid: encode the price using current px_exponent and tick_size.
  • Missing balance: ask Superluminal to confirm funding, then wait for UserCollateralUpdate or a fresh AccountSnapshot before trading.
  • Book reset: discard the affected book and resubscribe; the reference client does this automatically.

For complete message schemas and rejection reasons, use the public API reference.

docs.title: Getting Started with the Python Reference Client
docs.text:
The standalone Python reference client is a Textual terminal application for viewing native maker and taker books, monitoring a trading account, and submitting, modifying, and cancelling signed orders.

docs.text:
You need:

  • the Python reference client bundle (from the hosted documentation, unless this page is already inside that bundle);
  • Python 3.12 or newer;
  • internet access to install pinned dependencies from PyPI; and
  • a Solana-format Ed25519 keypair JSON file for your Fogo wallet.

The client is self-contained and installs into its own virtual environment. Before unpacking a hosted download, verify its checksum against the release manifest. If this page is inside an extracted bundle, continue with that enclosing bundle.

docs.title: Install the client
docs.text:
From python_gateway_client:

./scripts/bootstrap_venv.sh

This creates .venv locally and installs the pinned runtime dependencies. It does not modify the system Python installation.

Confirm the installed client before connecting:

./.venv/bin/sl-tui --version

docs.title: Fund the wallet
docs.text:
Request testnet collateral from Superluminal through your onboarding channel. Provide your public Fogo wallet address and intended subaccount, never your keypair. If asked to register an EVM deposit address, run the bundle's deposit:address command from funding-tools before starting the client. Its authenticated session would otherwise preempt the client's session.

See Funding accounts for the request, deposit-address, and balance-verification steps.

docs.title: Find active markets
docs.text:
Read symbology from the gateway's initial WebSocket snapshot before choosing --feed-id values.

At the time of writing, public testnet exposes BTC (1), ETH (2), and SOL (6). Treat the response as authoritative because markets and IDs may change.

Use px_exponent, tick_size, and size_decimals when converting human prices and quantities to raw wire integers.

docs.title: Start the TUI
docs.text:
From python_gateway_client:

./.venv/bin/sl-tui \
  --ws wss://testnet.slx.fi/ws \
  --keypair ./wallet.json \
  --subaccount 0 \
  --feed-id 1 \
  --feed-id 2 \
  --feed-id 6 \
  --partition-id 0x01

Arguments:

  • --ws: WebSocket endpoint. The default is local development, so always pass the public wss:// endpoint for testnet.
  • --keypair: Fogo wallet keypair JSON file.
  • --subaccount: trading subaccount displayed by the application.
  • --feed-id: market ID to subscribe to; repeat it for each market.
  • --partition-id: signed-message partition; public testnet uses 0x01.
  • --auth-expiry-seconds: authentication lifetime in seconds; the default is 0 (no session expiry). A nonzero value must be greater than 60.

docs.text:
The client performs these steps automatically:

  1. Read the initial WebSocket SymbologySnapshot.
  2. Send auth_wallet with the wallet public key.
  3. Sign the returned auth_challenge locally.
  4. Send auth_response and wait for ack accepted.
  5. Send subscribe_account.
  6. Subscribe to every configured market.

docs.text:
The order ticket creates and signs a signed_order proof locally. Choose:

  • market;
  • buy or sell;
  • quantity;
  • limit, mark-to-mid, or market order;
  • GTC or IOC where applicable; and
  • explicit MAKER or TAKER role.

  • ack rejected or ack busy reports a local command failure;

docs.title: Modify or cancel an order
docs.text: Press Modify beside a live GTC limit or mark-to-mid order. Edit its price or delta, and its remaining quantity, then press Apply Modify. Quantity may stay the same or decrease; increase it by cancelling and replacing the order. IOC and market orders cannot be modified. The client preserves the order's normal or reduce-only execution mode, including after reconnect. Press Cancel beside a working order to cancel it. Confirm ModifyAck, ModifyReject, CancelAck, or CancelReject on the account stream.

docs.title: TP/SL and reduce-only
docs.text:
Choose Reduce only under Execution to submit an ordinary reducing order. For TP/SL, choose the exit side, enter the protected Qty and a TP price, SL price, or both, choose Immediate or Parent fill, then press Create TP/SL. Each submission creates one group; repeat with different prices and quantities for multiple groups. Approved group IDs appear in Positions.

For Parent fill, wait for ConditionalApproved, enter its group ID, set the ordinary order ticket to the opposite side with quantity at least the group's, choose Normal execution, and press Submit Parent. One parent can bind to one group; only settled fills up to the group's quantity gain protection. Enter a group ID and press Cancel TP/SL to cancel a dormant group or an accepted active child. Confirm the lifecycle event on the account stream.

docs.title: Reuse the client modules
docs.text:
GatewayClient.submit_order accepts OrderDraft.execution_mode = ExecutionMode.REDUCE_ONLY. submit_conditional_group accepts a ConditionalGroupDraft for immediate or parent-fill protection; submit_conditional_parent binds a normal order after approval, and cancel_conditional_group cancels the group or active child. Account snapshots and conditional lifecycle events maintain subaccounts[].conditional_groups for reconnect reconciliation. See TP/SL and reduce-only.

The reference implementation is split into reusable modules under dfba_client:

  • GatewayClient handles authentication, subscriptions, orders, modifies, cancels, and subaccount transfers.
  • WebSocketTransport owns the reconnecting WebSocket loop.
  • commands contains JSON request encoders.
  • codec validates and decodes gateway messages.
  • signer loads keypairs and creates signed command proofs.

The TUI is an example consumer of these modules. Applications can construct a ClientConfig, initialize GatewayClient, and run WebSocketTransport without using Textual.
